question: 今度{こんど}の試験{しけん}の[[範囲]]は、教科書{きょうかしょ}の五十{ごじゅっ}ページまでです。
translation: The range (scope) of the next exam is up to page 50 of the textbook.
explanation: 範囲 is read はんい and means 'range, scope, extent' (試験の範囲 = the material an exam covers). 範 is read はん, as in 模範 もはん 'model, example' and 規範 きはん 'norm, standard'. 囲 is read い in on'yomi compounds such as 周囲 しゅうい 'surroundings' and 包囲 ほうい 'encirclement'; its kun'yomi is かこむ (囲む 'to surround'). The two traps are adding a dakuten to 範 (ばん) and adding an extra ん at the end (はんいん). Remember: it is simply は-ん-い, three sounds.
choice_notes: Wrong. 範 is read はん without a dakuten. ばん is the reading of other kanji such as 番 (番号 ばんごう) and 晩 (今晩 こんばん).
Wrong. There is no extra ん at the end. 囲 is read い, not いん. (はんいん is a different word: 班員 'group member'.)
Correct. はんい = 範囲 'range, scope'.
Wrong. へんい is the reading of 変異 'mutation, variation'. 範 is read はん, not へん.

vocab.example: できる範囲{はんい}で手伝{てつだ}います。
vocab.example_translation: I will help as much as I can (within the range of what I can do).

vocab.meaning: next time; this time; the upcoming (one)
vocab.example: 今度{こんど}の日曜日{にちようび}に映画{えいが}を見{み}に行{い}こう。
vocab.example_translation: Let's go see a movie this coming Sunday.

vocab.example: 来週{らいしゅう}、日本語{にほんご}の試験{しけん}がある。
vocab.example_translation: There is a Japanese exam next week.

vocab.example: 教科書{きょうかしょ}の十{じゅっ}ページを開{ひら}いてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please open your textbook to page 10.

vocab.example: 家族{かぞく}みんなでテーブルを囲{かこ}んだ。
vocab.example_translation: The whole family gathered around the table.

question: 彼{かれ}は仕事{しごと}の悩{なや}みを一人{ひとり}で[[抱えて]]いるようだ。
translation: It seems he is carrying his worries about work all by himself.
explanation: 抱えて is the て-form of 抱える（かかえる）, which means 'to hold in one's arms' and also 'to have (a problem, worry, debt) on one's hands'. 悩みを抱える 'to carry worries' and 問題を抱える 'to have a problem' are very common N2 phrases. The kanji 抱 has other readings too: だく and いだく (抱く 'to hug' / 'to harbor a hope'), and the on'yomi ほう (介抱 かいほう 'looking after a sick person'). But when the okurigana is える, 抱える is always read かかえる. The distractors are other common verbs that also end in -える, so learn each one with its own kanji.
choice_notes: Correct. かかえて = 抱えて, from 抱える 'to hold; to have (problems) on one's hands'.
Wrong. おさえて is 押さえて / 抑えて (押さえる 'to hold down', 抑える 'to suppress'). Different kanji.
Wrong. ささえて is 支えて (支える 'to support'). Different kanji.
Wrong. かまえて is 構えて (構える 'to set up; to take a stance'). Different kanji.

vocab.meaning: to hold in one's arms; to have (problems, worries) on one's hands
vocab.example: 大{おお}きな荷物{にもつ}を両手{りょうて}で抱{かか}えて歩{ある}いた。
vocab.example_translation: I walked carrying a big package in both arms.

vocab.example: 友達{ともだち}に悩{なや}みを相談{そうだん}した。
vocab.example_translation: I talked to a friend about my worries.

vocab.example: 家族{かぞく}が私{わたし}の生活{せいかつ}を支{ささ}えてくれた。
vocab.example_translation: My family supported me in my daily life.

vocab.meaning: to suppress, to hold back (feelings, prices)
vocab.example: 怒{いか}りを抑{おさ}えるのは難{むずか}しい。
vocab.example_translation: It is hard to hold back anger.

vocab.meaning: to set up (a shop, a house); to take a stance
vocab.example: 駅前{えきまえ}に店{みせ}を構{かま}える。
vocab.example_translation: To set up a shop in front of the station.

grammar.meaning: it seems that ~, it looks like ~ (a guess based on what you see or feel)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj + な / noun + の + ようだ
grammar.example: 外{そと}は雨{あめ}が降{ふ}っているようだ。
grammar.example_translation: It seems to be raining outside.

question: 留学中{りゅうがくちゅう}に、とても[[貴重]]な経験{けいけん}をすることができた。
translation: During my study abroad, I was able to have a very valuable experience.
explanation: 貴重 is read きちょう and means 'valuable, precious'. 貴 is read き, as in 貴族 きぞく 'aristocrat'. 重 has two common on'yomi: じゅう (重要 じゅうよう 'important', 体重 たいじゅう 'body weight') and ちょう (慎重 しんちょう 'careful', 尊重 そんちょう 'respect'). In 貴重 it is ちょう with a long vowel. Typical traps are the じゅう reading of 重, a voiced ぎ, and dropping the long vowel (きちょ).
choice_notes: Wrong. じゅう is another reading of 重 (重要 じゅうよう), but 貴重 uses ちょう.
Wrong. ぎちょう is 議長 'chairperson'. 貴 is read き, without a dakuten.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: it must be ちょう, not ちょ.
Correct. きちょう = 貴重 'valuable, precious'.

vocab.example: 貴重{きちょう}な時間{じかん}を割{さ}いていただき、ありがとうございます。
vocab.example_translation: Thank you for sparing your valuable time.

vocab.example: 来年{らいねん}、アメリカに留学{りゅうがく}するつもりだ。
vocab.example_translation: I plan to study abroad in America next year.

vocab.example: 授業中{じゅぎょうちゅう}は携帯電話{けいたいでんわ}を使{つか}わないでください。
vocab.example_translation: Please do not use your mobile phone during class.

vocab.example: 海外{かいがい}で働{はたら}いた経験{けいけん}がありますか。
vocab.example_translation: Do you have experience working abroad?

grammar.meaning: can ~, to be able to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができる
grammar.example: この図書館{としょかん}では本{ほん}を二週間{にしゅうかん}借{か}りることができる。
grammar.example_translation: At this library you can borrow books for two weeks.

question: 最近{さいきん}、この道{みち}では事故{じこ}が[[頻繁]]に起{お}きている。
translation: Recently, accidents have been happening frequently on this road.
explanation: 頻繁 is read ひんぱん and means 'frequent'. 頻 is read ひん, as in 頻度 ひんど 'frequency' and 頻出 ひんしゅつ 'appearing frequently'. 繁 is normally read はん, as in 繁栄 はんえい 'prosperity' and 繁華街 はんかがい 'busy downtown area', but after ん it changes to ぱん (with the small circle, handakuten) in this word. So the traps are: ばん (dakuten instead of handakuten), びん (wrong first sound), and はん (forgetting the sound change).
choice_notes: Wrong. 繁 changes to ぱん (handakuten ゜), not ばん (dakuten ゛).
Correct. ひんぱん = 頻繁 'frequent'.
Wrong. 頻 is read ひん, not びん. びん is the reading of 便 in 郵便 ゆうびん.
Wrong. The sound change is missing. In 頻繁, は becomes ぱ after ん.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}とは頻繁{ひんぱん}にメールで連絡{れんらく}を取{と}っている。
vocab.example_translation: I am in frequent contact with him by email.

vocab.example: 最近{さいきん}、よく眠{ねむ}れない。
vocab.example_translation: Recently I can't sleep well.

vocab.example: 駅{えき}の近{ちか}くで交通事故{こうつうじこ}があった。
vocab.example_translation: There was a traffic accident near the station.

vocab.meaning: to happen, to occur (also: to get up)
vocab.example: 夜中{よなか}に大{おお}きな地震{じしん}が起{お}きた。
vocab.example_translation: A big earthquake happened in the middle of the night.

grammar.meaning: turns a な-adjective into an adverb ('~ly')
grammar.formation: な-adjective + に + verb (頻繁 → 頻繁に起きる)
grammar.example: 図書館{としょかん}では静{しず}かに話{はな}してください。
grammar.example_translation: Please speak quietly in the library.

question: 忙{いそが}しくて外食{がいしょく}ばかりしていると、栄養{えいよう}が[[偏り]]がちだ。
translation: If you are busy and eat out all the time, your diet tends to become unbalanced.
explanation: 偏り is the masu-stem of 偏る（かたよる）'to lean to one side, to be unbalanced, to be biased'. Here it is followed by 〜がち 'tend to', so 偏りがち means 'tends to become unbalanced'. 栄養が偏る 'one's nutrition is unbalanced' is a set phrase. The on'yomi of 偏 is へん, as in 偏見 へんけん 'prejudice' and 偏差値 へんさち 'standard score'. The distractors are words that sound similar: かたまり 'lump', たより 'reliance / news', and まがり 'bend'.
choice_notes: Wrong. かたまり is 固まり / 塊 'lump, mass', from 固まる 'to harden'.
Correct. かたより = 偏り, from 偏る 'to be unbalanced, biased'.
Wrong. たより is 頼り 'reliance' (from 頼る) or 便り 'news, letter'. It is missing the かた at the start.
Wrong. まがり is 曲がり 'bend, curve', from 曲がる 'to turn, to bend'.

vocab.meaning: to lean to one side, to be unbalanced, to be biased
vocab.example: 彼{かれ}の意見{いけん}は少{すこ}し偏{かたよ}っている。
vocab.example_translation: His opinion is a little biased.

vocab.example: 週末{しゅうまつ}は家族{かぞく}で外食{がいしょく}することが多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: On weekends we often eat out as a family.

vocab.example: 子{こ}どもには栄養{えいよう}のある食事{しょくじ}が必要{ひつよう}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Children need nutritious meals.

vocab.meaning: to harden, to set; to be settled
vocab.example: セメントが固{かた}まるまで待{ま}つ。
vocab.example_translation: Wait until the cement hardens.

vocab.meaning: to rely on, to depend on
vocab.example: 親{おや}に頼{たよ}らずに生活{せいかつ}したい。
vocab.example_translation: I want to live without depending on my parents.

grammar.meaning: tend to ~, be apt to ~ (usually something negative)
grammar.formation: Verb masu-stem / noun + がち（だ）
grammar.example: 冬{ふゆ}は運動不足{うんどうぶそく}になりがちだ。
grammar.example_translation: In winter we tend not to get enough exercise.

grammar.meaning: nothing but ~, only ~ (with a feeling of 'too much')
grammar.formation: Noun + ばかり + verb / Verb て-form + ばかりいる
grammar.example: 弟{おとうと}はゲームばかりしている。
grammar.example_translation: My younger brother does nothing but play games.

grammar.meaning: if ~ / whenever ~ (a natural or automatic result follows)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ている form + と
grammar.example: 春{はる}になると、桜{さくら}が咲{さ}く。
grammar.example_translation: When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.

question: 図書館{としょかん}から、借{か}りた本{ほん}を早{はや}く返{かえ}すように[[催促]]された。
translation: The library pressed me to return the books I had borrowed soon.
explanation: 催促 is read さいそく and means 'pressing, urging, a reminder to do something (pay, reply, return)'. 催 is read さい, as in 開催 かいさい 'holding (an event)' and 主催 しゅさい 'hosting, organizing (an event)'; its kun'yomi is もよおす (催す 'to hold an event'). 促 is read そく, as in 促進 そくしん 'promotion'; its kun'yomi is うながす (促す 'to urge'). The trap is the voiced ぞく (which belongs to kanji like 続 and 族) and the similar-sounding real word 菜食 さいしょく.
choice_notes: Wrong. 促 is read そく without a dakuten. ぞく is the reading of 続 (継続 けいぞく) or 族 (家族 かぞく).
Wrong. さいしょく is 菜食 'vegetarian diet'. 促 is not read しょく.
Wrong. 催 is read さい, so the い is missing.
Correct. さいそく = 催促 'pressing, urging'.

vocab.meaning: pressing (someone to do something), urging, demand
vocab.example: 家賃{やちん}の支払{しはら}いを催促{さいそく}された。
vocab.example_translation: I was pressed to pay the rent.

vocab.example: 図書館{としょかん}で静{しず}かに勉強{べんきょう}した。
vocab.example_translation: I studied quietly in the library.

vocab.example: 借{か}りたお金{かね}は必{かなら}ず返{かえ}します。
vocab.example_translation: I will definitely pay back the money I borrowed.

vocab.example: オリンピックが東京{とうきょう}で開催{かいさい}された。
vocab.example_translation: The Olympics were held in Tokyo.

vocab.meaning: to urge, to prompt, to encourage
vocab.example: 先生{せんせい}は学生{がくせい}に発言{はつげん}を促{うなが}した。
vocab.example_translation: The teacher encouraged the students to speak up.

grammar.pattern: 〜ように言う / 頼む / 催促する
grammar.meaning: to tell / ask / press someone to do ~ (reported request)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない form + ように + 言う・頼む・催促する
grammar.example: 先生{せんせい}に毎日{まいにち}復習{ふくしゅう}するように言{い}われた。
grammar.example_translation: My teacher told me to review every day.

grammar.meaning: to be ~ed (something is done to the subject)
grammar.formation: Group 1: ない-stem + れる (言う → 言われる); Group 2: stem + られる; する → される
grammar.example: 先生{せんせい}に褒{ほ}められた。
grammar.example_translation: I was praised by my teacher.

question: 会社{かいしゃ}は経費{けいひ}を[[削減]]するため、出張{しゅっちょう}の回数{かいすう}を減{へ}らした。
translation: To cut expenses, the company reduced the number of business trips.
explanation: 削減 is read さくげん and means 'reduction, cut' (経費削減 'cost cutting'). 削 is read さく, as in 削除 さくじょ 'deletion'; its kun'yomi is けずる (削る 'to shave, to cut down'). 減 is read げん, as in 減少 げんしょう 'decrease' and 増減 ぞうげん 'increase and decrease'; its kun'yomi is へる / へらす (減る, 減らす), which also appears in this sentence. Watch out for similar-looking kanji: 削 looks like 消 (しょう, as in 消費 しょうひ) because both contain 肖, and 減 looks like 感 (かん) because both contain 咸.
choice_notes: Correct. さくげん = 削減 'reduction, cut'.
Wrong. There is no small っ here, and 減 is the voiced げん, not けん.
Wrong. しょうげん is 証言 'testimony'. しょう is the reading of the similar-looking kanji 消, not 削.
Wrong. 減 is read げん. かん is the reading of the similar-looking kanji 感 (感動 かんどう).

vocab.example: 政府{せいふ}は予算{よさん}を一割{いちわり}削減{さくげん}した。
vocab.example_translation: The government cut the budget by ten percent.

vocab.example: 交通費{こうつうひ}は会社{かいしゃ}の経費{けいひ}で払{はら}われる。
vocab.example_translation: Transportation costs are paid as company expenses.

vocab.example: 来週{らいしゅう}、大阪{おおさか}へ出張{しゅっちょう}する。
vocab.example_translation: I am going on a business trip to Osaka next week.

vocab.example: 一日{いちにち}に歯{は}を磨{みが}く回数{かいすう}は何回{なんかい}ですか。
vocab.example_translation: How many times a day do you brush your teeth?

vocab.example: 健康{けんこう}のために砂糖{さとう}を減{へ}らしている。
vocab.example_translation: I am cutting down on sugar for my health.

grammar.meaning: in order to ~, for the purpose of ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + の + ため（に）
grammar.example: 家{いえ}を買{か}うために貯金{ちょきん}している。
grammar.example_translation: I am saving money in order to buy a house.

question: どんなに小{ちい}さな努力{どりょく}でも、[[継続]]すれば大{おお}きな力{ちから}になる。
translation: No matter how small an effort is, if you keep it up, it becomes a great strength.
explanation: 継続 is read けいぞく and means 'continuation'. 継 is read けい, as in 中継 ちゅうけい 'relay broadcast' and 後継者 こうけいしゃ 'successor'; its kun'yomi is つぐ (継ぐ 'to succeed to, to inherit'). 続 is read ぞく with a dakuten in on'yomi compounds: 連続 れんぞく 'in a row', 相続 そうぞく 'inheritance', 持続 じぞく 'sustaining'; its kun'yomi is つづく (続く). The main trap is the unvoiced そく, which makes the different word 計測 けいそく 'measurement'. Also keep the long vowel けい.
choice_notes: Wrong. けいそく is 計測 'measurement'. 続 is read with a dakuten: ぞく.
Wrong. けいしょく is 軽食 'light meal'. 続 is not read しょく.
Correct. けいぞく = 継続 'continuation'.
Wrong. 継 is read けい, so the い is missing.

vocab.example: 会社{かいしゃ}との契約{けいやく}を継続{けいぞく}することにした。
vocab.example_translation: I decided to continue the contract with the company.

vocab.example: 彼女{かのじょ}は努力{どりょく}して医者{いしゃ}になった。
vocab.example_translation: She worked hard and became a doctor.

vocab.example: 困{こま}っている人{ひと}の力{ちから}になりたい。
vocab.example_translation: I want to be of help to people in trouble.

vocab.example: 雨{あめ}が三日{みっか}も続{つづ}いている。
vocab.example_translation: The rain has continued for three whole days.

grammar.pattern: どんなに〜ても / でも
grammar.meaning: no matter how ~
grammar.formation: どんなに + Verb て-form + も / い-adj くても / な-adj・noun + でも
grammar.example: どんなに忙{いそが}しくても、朝{あさ}ご飯{はん}は食{た}べる。
grammar.example_translation: No matter how busy I am, I eat breakfast.

grammar.meaning: if ~
grammar.formation: Group 1: change the final う-sound to え + ば (行く → 行けば); Group 2: stem + れば; する → すれば; くる → くれば
grammar.example: 急{いそ}げば間{ま}に合{あ}う。
grammar.example_translation: If you hurry, you will make it in time.

question: このズボンは腰{こし}の部分{ぶぶん}が少{すこ}し[[緩い]]。
translation: These trousers are a little loose around the waist.
explanation: 緩い is read ゆるい and means 'loose, slack', and also 'gentle (slope)' or 'lenient (rules)': 緩い坂 'a gentle slope', 規則が緩い 'the rules are lax'. Related verbs: 緩む ゆるむ 'to come loose' and 緩める ゆるめる 'to loosen'. The on'yomi is かん, as in 緩和 かんわ 'easing, relief'. All the distractors are real i-adjectives ending in -るい, so this question tests whether you have connected 緩 with ゆる-.
choice_notes: Wrong. ぬるい means 'lukewarm' (お湯がぬるい). It is usually written in hiragana or as 温い.
Wrong. かるい is 軽い 'light (in weight)'.
Wrong. ずるい means 'sly, unfair, cunning'. It is usually written in hiragana.
Correct. ゆるい = 緩い 'loose'.

vocab.example: この学校{がっこう}は校則{こうそく}が緩{ゆる}い。
vocab.example_translation: This school's rules are lax.

vocab.example: 重{おも}い物{もの}を持{も}って腰{こし}を痛{いた}めた。
vocab.example_translation: I hurt my lower back carrying something heavy.

vocab.example: この部分{ぶぶん}をもう一度{いちど}説明{せつめい}してください。
vocab.example_translation: Please explain this part once more.

vocab.example: 新{あたら}しいズボンを買{か}った。
vocab.example_translation: I bought new trousers.

vocab.meaning: to loosen, to relax, to slow down
vocab.example: 暑{あつ}いのでネクタイを緩{ゆる}めた。
vocab.example_translation: It was hot, so I loosened my tie.

question: 予定{よてい}が変{か}わっても、[[柔軟]]に対応{たいおう}できる人{ひと}が求{もと}められている。
translation: People who can respond flexibly even when plans change are in demand.
explanation: 柔軟 is read じゅうなん and means 'flexible, pliable' (柔軟な考え方 'flexible thinking', 柔軟に対応する 'respond flexibly'). 柔 is usually read じゅう, as in 柔道 じゅうどう 'judo'; it has a rare second on'yomi にゅう (柔和 にゅうわ 'gentle'), which is the trap in にゅうなん. 軟 is read なん, as in 軟弱 なんじゃく 'weak, soft'. Both kanji have the kun'yomi やわらかい (柔らかい, 軟らかい 'soft'). Also watch the long vowel: じゅう, not じゅ.
choice_notes: Wrong. じゅなん is 受難 'suffering, ordeal'. 柔 needs the long vowel: じゅう.
Correct. じゅうなん = 柔軟 'flexible'.
Wrong. にゅう is a rare reading of 柔 (柔和 にゅうわ 'gentle'), but 柔軟 uses じゅう.
Wrong. 軟 is read なん. らん is the reading of kanji such as 乱 (混乱 こんらん) and 覧.

vocab.example: 体{からだ}を柔軟{じゅうなん}にするためにストレッチをする。
vocab.example_translation: I stretch to make my body flexible.

vocab.example: 週末{しゅうまつ}の予定{よてい}はもう決{き}まった。
vocab.example_translation: My plans for the weekend are already decided.

vocab.example: 信号{しんごう}が赤{あか}から青{あお}に変{か}わった。
vocab.example_translation: The traffic light changed from red to green.

vocab.example: お客様{きゃくさま}の質問{しつもん}に丁寧{ていねい}に対応{たいおう}する。
vocab.example_translation: We respond politely to customers' questions.

vocab.meaning: to seek, to request, to look for
vocab.example: 会社{かいしゃ}は経験{けいけん}のある人{ひと}を求{もと}めている。
vocab.example_translation: The company is looking for people with experience.

grammar.meaning: even if ~, even when ~
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + も / い-adj くても / な-adj・noun + でも
grammar.example: 雨{あめ}が降{ふ}っても、試合{しあい}は行{おこな}われる。
grammar.example_translation: Even if it rains, the match will be held.

grammar.meaning: is being ~ed / is ~ed (a general or ongoing situation)
grammar.formation: Passive verb て-form + いる (求める → 求められている)
grammar.example: この本{ほん}は世界中{せかいじゅう}で読{よ}まれている。
grammar.example_translation: This book is read all over the world.

question: 来週{らいしゅう}、取引先{とりひきさき}の会社{かいしゃ}を[[訪問]]する予定{よてい}だ。
translation: Next week I plan to visit a client's company.
explanation: 訪問 is read ほうもん and means 'visit' (家庭訪問 'home visit'). 訪 is read ほう, as in 来訪 らいほう 'visit (to here)'; its kun'yomi are たずねる (訪ねる 'to visit') and おとずれる (訪れる 'to visit, to arrive'). 問 is read もん, as in 質問 しつもん and 問題 もんだい. Kanji with the part 方 are usually read ほう or ぼう: 訪・方・放 are ほう, but 防・妨・坊 are ぼう. That is why ぼうもん is a tempting trap.
choice_notes: Correct. ほうもん = 訪問 'visit'.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 訪 is ほう, not ほ.
Wrong. 訪 is read ほう without a dakuten. ぼう is the reading of the similar-looking kanji 防 (防止 ぼうし) and 妨 (妨害 ぼうがい).
Wrong. 問 is read もん. むん is not a reading of 問.

vocab.example: 先生{せんせい}が生徒{せいと}の家{いえ}を訪問{ほうもん}した。
vocab.example_translation: The teacher visited the student's home.

vocab.example: 取引先{とりひきさき}との会議{かいぎ}は午後{ごご}三時{さんじ}からだ。
vocab.example_translation: The meeting with the client is from 3 p.m.

vocab.example: 今年{ことし}の夏{なつ}は北海道{ほっかいどう}を旅行{りょこう}する予定{よてい}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This summer I plan to travel around Hokkaido.

vocab.example: 久{ひさ}しぶりに祖母{そぼ}の家{いえ}を訪{たず}ねた。
vocab.example_translation: I visited my grandmother's house for the first time in a long while.

grammar.meaning: to plan to ~, to be scheduled to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + の + 予定だ
grammar.example: 会議{かいぎ}は十時{じゅうじ}に始{はじ}まる予定{よてい}だ。
grammar.example_translation: The meeting is scheduled to start at ten.

question: 私{わたし}は運動神経{うんどうしんけい}が[[鈍い]]ので、球技{きゅうぎ}が苦手{にがて}だ。
translation: I have poor reflexes (I'm not athletic), so I'm bad at ball games.
explanation: 鈍い is read にぶい and means 'dull, blunt, slow (to react)': 運動神経が鈍い 'not athletic', 反応が鈍い 'slow to react', 鈍い痛み 'a dull pain'. Its opposite is 鋭い するどい 'sharp'. The related verb is 鈍る にぶる 'to become dull'. The on'yomi is どん, as in 鈍感 どんかん 'insensitive' and 鈍行 どんこう 'local (slow) train'. (In some contexts 鈍い can also be read のろい 'sluggish', but にぶい is the standard reading.) The distractors are other i-adjectives that sound similar; note that にがい 'bitter' is written 苦い, the same kanji as 苦手 in this sentence.
choice_notes: Wrong. しぶい is 渋い 'astringent (taste); tasteful, sober (style)'.
Wrong. にがい is 苦い 'bitter'. Its kanji 苦 appears in 苦手 in this sentence, which can mislead you.
Correct. にぶい = 鈍い 'dull, slow'.
Wrong. にくい is 憎い 'hateful'.

vocab.example: このナイフは切{き}れ味{あじ}が鈍{にぶ}い。
vocab.example_translation: This knife does not cut well (it is dull).

vocab.example: 兄{あに}は運動神経{うんどうしんけい}がよくて、何{なん}でもすぐにできる。
vocab.example_translation: My older brother is athletic and can do any sport right away.

vocab.example: サッカーや野球{やきゅう}などの球技{きゅうぎ}が好{す}きだ。
vocab.example_translation: I like ball sports such as soccer and baseball.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}は人前{ひとまえ}で話{はな}すのが苦手{にがて}だ。
vocab.example_translation: I am bad at speaking in front of people.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は人{ひと}の気持{きも}ちに鈍感{どんかん}だ。
vocab.example_translation: He is insensitive to other people's feelings.

grammar.meaning: because ~, since ~ (softer and more polite than から)
grammar.formation: Plain form + ので (な-adj / noun + なので)
grammar.example: 雨{あめ}が降{ふ}っているので、出{で}かけない。
grammar.example_translation: Since it is raining, I won't go out.

question: 新{あたら}しい部長{ぶちょう}は、まず部下{ぶか}の仕事{しごと}の状況{じょうきょう}を[[把握]]しようとした。
translation: The new department manager first tried to get a grasp of his staff's work situation.
explanation: 把握 is read はあく and means 'grasp, understanding (of a situation)'. 状況を把握する 'to grasp the situation' is a very common phrase in business and news. 把 is read は. 握 is read あく, as in 握手 あくしゅ 'handshake'; its kun'yomi is にぎる (握る 'to grip'). The big trap: the right side of 握 is 屋, which is read おく (屋上 おくじょう 'rooftop'), so learners often guess はおく. Also, 把 has no dakuten here.
choice_notes: Wrong. おく is the reading of 屋, which is only a part of 握. 握 itself is read あく.
Correct. はあく = 把握 'grasp, understanding'.
Wrong. 把 is read は without a dakuten.
Wrong. はやく is 早く / 速く 'early, quickly'. It is not a reading of 把握.

vocab.example: 地図{ちず}を見{み}て、町{まち}の全体{ぜんたい}を把握{はあく}した。
vocab.example_translation: I looked at the map and got an overall picture of the town.

vocab.meaning: department manager, head of a department
vocab.example: 部長{ぶちょう}に会議{かいぎ}の資料{しりょう}を渡{わた}した。
vocab.example_translation: I handed the meeting materials to the department manager.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は部下{ぶか}にとても優{やさ}しい。
vocab.example_translation: He is very kind to his staff.

vocab.example: 現在{げんざい}の状況{じょうきょう}を詳{くわ}しく説明{せつめい}してください。
vocab.example_translation: Please explain the current situation in detail.

vocab.meaning: to grip, to grasp, to hold
vocab.example: 子{こ}どもが母親{ははおや}の手{て}をしっかり握{にぎ}った。
vocab.example_translation: The child held its mother's hand tightly.

grammar.meaning: to try to ~, to attempt to ~; to be about to ~
grammar.formation: Verb volitional form + とする (する → しようとする)
grammar.example: 家{いえ}を出{で}ようとしたとき、電話{でんわ}が鳴{な}った。
grammar.example_translation: Just as I was about to leave the house, the phone rang.

question: 大雨{おおあめ}のため、市{し}は住民{じゅうみん}を避難{ひなん}させる[[措置]]をとった。
translation: Because of the heavy rain, the city took measures to evacuate residents.
explanation: 措置 is read そち and means 'measure, step (taken to deal with a situation)'. 措置をとる 'to take measures' is the set phrase. 措 is read そ and appears almost only in this word. 置 is read ち, as in 位置 いち 'position', 放置 ほうち 'leaving as is', and 設置 せっち 'installation'; its kun'yomi is おく (置く). Two real words make good traps: 処置 しょち 'treatment, handling' has a similar meaning, and 装置 そうち means 'device'.
choice_notes: Wrong. しょち is 処置 'treatment, handling' (応急処置 'first aid'). 措 is read そ, not しょ.
Wrong. そうち is 装置 'device, equipment'. 措 is a short そ.
Wrong. 置 is read ち without a dakuten.
Correct. そち = 措置 'measure, step'.

vocab.meaning: measure, step, action (taken to deal with something)
vocab.example: 政府{せいふ}は物価{ぶっか}の上昇{じょうしょう}に対{たい}して特別{とくべつ}な措置{そち}をとった。
vocab.example_translation: The government took special measures against rising prices.

vocab.example: 大雨{おおあめ}で電車{でんしゃ}が止{と}まった。
vocab.example_translation: The trains stopped because of heavy rain.

vocab.example: この町{まち}の住民{じゅうみん}は約{やく}一万人{いちまんにん}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This town has about ten thousand residents.

vocab.example: 地震{じしん}のあと、近{ちか}くの学校{がっこう}に避難{ひなん}した。
vocab.example_translation: After the earthquake, we took refuge in a nearby school.

vocab.example: 医者{いしゃ}がけがの応急処置{おうきゅうしょち}をした。
vocab.example_translation: The doctor gave first aid for the injury.

grammar.meaning: because of ~, due to ~ (formal)
grammar.formation: Noun + のため / plain form + ため
grammar.example: 事故{じこ}のため、電車{でんしゃ}が遅{おく}れています。
grammar.example_translation: Due to an accident, the trains are delayed.

grammar.meaning: to make / let someone do ~
grammar.formation: Group 1: ない-stem + せる (行く → 行かせる); Group 2: stem + させる; する → させる
grammar.example: 母{はは}は弟{おとうと}に部屋{へや}を掃除{そうじ}させた。
grammar.example_translation: My mother made my younger brother clean his room.

question: 締{し}め切{き}りが[[迫って]]いるので、今夜{こんや}は遅{おそ}くまで仕事{しごと}をするつもりだ。
translation: The deadline is approaching, so I intend to work until late tonight.
explanation: 迫って is the て-form of 迫る（せまる）'to approach, to draw near (a time, danger)'; it can also mean 'to press someone (for an answer)'. 締め切りが迫る 'a deadline approaches' and 危険が迫る 'danger approaches' are typical. The on'yomi of 迫 is はく, as in 迫力 はくりょく 'impact, power' and 圧迫 あっぱく 'pressure'. The trap せめて looks very similar (せま- vs せめ-), but it has no small っ and comes from a different verb (責める / 攻める). しまって is tempting because the word 締め切り in the same sentence uses 締 (締まる しまる).
choice_notes: Wrong. せめて is the て-form of 責める 'to blame' / 攻める 'to attack' (it is also an adverb 'at least').
Wrong. しまって is 閉まって / 締まって 'to close, to tighten'. Different kanji.
Correct. せまって = 迫って, from 迫る 'to approach, to draw near'.
Wrong. つまって is 詰まって 'to be blocked, to be packed'. Different kanji.

vocab.meaning: to approach, to draw near; to press (someone for something)
vocab.example: 台風{たいふう}が九州{きゅうしゅう}に迫{せま}っている。
vocab.example_translation: A typhoon is approaching Kyushu.

vocab.example: レポートの締{し}め切{き}りは金曜日{きんようび}だ。
vocab.example_translation: The report deadline is Friday.

vocab.example: 今夜{こんや}は月{つき}がきれいだ。
vocab.example_translation: The moon is beautiful tonight.

vocab.meaning: impact, force, power (of a film, performance, etc.)
vocab.example: この映画{えいが}は迫力{はくりょく}がある。
vocab.example_translation: This film is powerful.

vocab.example: 失敗{しっぱい}した人{ひと}を責{せ}めてはいけない。
vocab.example_translation: You must not blame people who failed.

grammar.meaning: to intend to ~, to plan to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない form + つもりだ
grammar.example: 夏休{なつやす}みに国{くに}へ帰{かえ}るつもりだ。
grammar.example_translation: I intend to go back to my country during the summer vacation.

grammar.meaning: because ~, since ~
grammar.formation: Plain form + ので (な-adj / noun + なので)
grammar.example: 熱{ねつ}があるので、今日{きょう}は休{やす}みます。
grammar.example_translation: I have a fever, so I will take today off.

question: 長時間{ちょうじかん}悪{わる}い[[姿勢]]で座{すわ}っていると、腰{こし}が痛{いた}くなる。
translation: If you sit in a bad posture for a long time, your lower back starts to hurt.
explanation: 姿勢 is read しせい and has two meanings: 'posture' (姿勢がいい 'good posture') and 'attitude, stance' (前向きな姿勢 'a positive attitude'). 姿 is read し, as in 容姿 ようし 'appearance'; its kun'yomi is すがた (姿 'figure, appearance'). 勢 is usually read せい, as in 勢力 せいりょく 'influence' and 情勢 じょうせい 'situation'; its kun'yomi is いきおい (勢い 'force, momentum'). The trap: in 大勢 おおぜい 'many people', 勢 becomes ぜい, but in 姿勢 it stays unvoiced せい.
choice_notes: Correct. しせい = 姿勢 'posture; attitude'.
Wrong. ぜい is the reading of 勢 only in words like 大勢 おおぜい. In 姿勢 it is せい.
Wrong. じせい is 時勢 'trend of the times' or 自制 'self-control'. 姿 is read し, without a dakuten.
Wrong. 勢 is read せい, so the final い is missing.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は仕事{しごと}に対{たい}して真剣{しんけん}な姿勢{しせい}を見{み}せた。
vocab.example_translation: He showed a serious attitude toward his work.

vocab.example: 長時間{ちょうじかん}パソコンを使{つか}うと目{め}が疲{つか}れる。
vocab.example_translation: Using a computer for long hours makes your eyes tired.

vocab.example: どうぞ、こちらに座{すわ}ってください。
vocab.example_translation: Please have a seat here.

vocab.example: 腰{こし}が痛{いた}くて歩{ある}けない。
vocab.example_translation: My lower back hurts so much that I can't walk.

vocab.example: 駅前{えきまえ}に大勢{おおぜい}の人{ひと}が集{あつ}まっていた。
vocab.example_translation: A crowd of people had gathered in front of the station.

grammar.meaning: if ~ / whenever ~ (a natural result follows)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ている form + と
grammar.example: このボタンを押{お}すと、ドアが開{ひら}く。
grammar.example_translation: If you press this button, the door opens.

grammar.meaning: to become ~ (change of state with an い-adjective)
grammar.formation: い-adjective without い + くなる (痛い → 痛くなる)
grammar.example: 秋{あき}になると、日{ひ}が短{みじか}くなる。
grammar.example_translation: When autumn comes, the days get shorter.

question: お忙{いそが}しいところ[[恐縮]]ですが、こちらの書類{しょるい}をご確認{かくにん}いただけますか。
translation: I'm sorry to trouble you when you are busy, but could you please check these documents?
explanation: 恐縮 is read きょうしゅく. It expresses feeling sorry or grateful for troubling someone, and 恐縮ですが 'I'm sorry to trouble you, but...' is a standard polite phrase in business Japanese. 恐 is read きょう, as in 恐怖 きょうふ 'fear'; its kun'yomi are おそれる (恐れる 'to fear') and おそろしい (恐ろしい 'frightening'). 縮 is read しゅく, as in 短縮 たんしゅく 'shortening'; its kun'yomi is ちぢむ (縮む 'to shrink'). The traps change only one sound: しゅう or しょく instead of しゅく, or a short きょ.
choice_notes: Wrong. きょうしゅう is 郷愁 'nostalgia' or 教習 'driving lessons, training'. 縮 is read しゅく, not しゅう.
Wrong. 恐 needs the long vowel: きょう, not きょ.
Wrong. きょうしょく is 教職 'the teaching profession'. 縮 is read しゅく, not しょく.
Correct. きょうしゅく = 恐縮 'being sorry/grateful for the trouble'.

vocab.meaning: being sorry (or grateful) for troubling someone (very polite)
vocab.example: わざわざ来{き}ていただいて恐縮{きょうしゅく}です。
vocab.example_translation: I am very grateful (and sorry) that you came all this way.

vocab.example: 必要{ひつよう}な書類{しょるい}をそろえて提出{ていしゅつ}した。
vocab.example_translation: I gathered the necessary documents and submitted them.

vocab.example: 出{で}かける前{まえ}に、窓{まど}が閉{し}まっているか確認{かくにん}した。
vocab.example_translation: Before going out, I checked that the windows were closed.

vocab.example: 今週{こんしゅう}は仕事{しごと}がとても忙{いそが}しい。
vocab.example_translation: Work is very busy this week.

grammar.meaning: when you are busy (a polite fixed phrase used before a request or thanks)
grammar.formation: Fixed phrase, not freely formed with any adjective: お忙しいところ（を）. Similar set phrases: お疲れのところ, お休みのところ, お急ぎのところ, ご多忙のところ
grammar.example: お忙{いそが}しいところ、お越{こ}しいただきありがとうございます。
grammar.example_translation: Thank you for coming when you are so busy.

grammar.pattern: ご〜いただけますか / お〜いただけますか
grammar.meaning: could you please ~? (very polite request)
grammar.formation: ご + suru-noun + いただけますか / お + Verb masu-stem + いただけますか
grammar.example: こちらにお名前{なまえ}をご記入{きにゅう}いただけますか。
grammar.example_translation: Could you please write your name here?

question: 決勝戦{けっしょうせん}で、私{わたし}たちのチームは相手{あいて}に[[圧倒]]された。
translation: In the final, our team was overwhelmed by the opponent.
explanation: 圧倒 is read あっとう and means 'overwhelming, overpowering'; 圧倒的 あっとうてき means 'overwhelming'. 圧 is read あつ, as in 圧力 あつりょく 'pressure' and 気圧 きあつ 'air pressure'. When あつ comes before a k-, s-, t- or h- sound, it shrinks to あっ (small っ), and a following h- sound changes to p-: 圧倒 あっとう, 圧勝 あっしょう 'overwhelming victory', 圧迫 あっぱく 'pressure' (迫 はく → ぱく). 倒 is read とう, as in 倒産 とうさん 'bankruptcy'; its kun'yomi is たおれる (倒れる 'to fall down'). So remember three things: small っ, unvoiced と, and a long vowel とう.
choice_notes: Correct. あっとう = 圧倒 'overwhelming'.
Wrong. The small っ is missing. あつ becomes あっ before と.
Wrong. 倒 is read とう without a dakuten.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 倒 is とう. (あっと is a different word, an adverb meaning 'with a gasp', as in あっと驚く 'to gasp in surprise'.)

vocab.example: 山{やま}の上{うえ}から見{み}た景色{けしき}の美{うつく}しさに圧倒{あっとう}された。
vocab.example_translation: I was overwhelmed by the beauty of the view from the top of the mountain.

vocab.example: 決勝戦{けっしょうせん}は日曜日{にちようび}に行{おこな}われる。
vocab.example_translation: The final will be held on Sunday.

vocab.example: 話{はな}すときは相手{あいて}の目{め}を見{み}なさい。
vocab.example_translation: Look the other person in the eyes when you talk.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は圧倒的{あっとうてき}な強{つよ}さで優勝{ゆうしょう}した。
vocab.example_translation: He won the championship with overwhelming strength.

vocab.example: 強{つよ}い風{かぜ}で木{き}が倒{たお}れた。
vocab.example_translation: The tree fell down in the strong wind.

grammar.meaning: to be ~ed (by someone)
grammar.formation: Group 1: ない-stem + れる; Group 2: stem + られる; する → される (圧倒する → 圧倒される)
grammar.example: 私{わたし}は先生{せんせい}に名前{なまえ}を呼{よ}ばれた。
grammar.example_translation: My name was called by the teacher.

question: 注意{ちゅうい}を[[怠った]]ために、大{おお}きな事故{じこ}が起{お}きてしまった。
translation: Because someone neglected to pay attention, a serious accident happened.
explanation: 怠った is the past form of 怠る（おこたる）'to neglect, to fail to do (a duty)': 注意を怠る 'to be careless', 努力を怠る 'to slack off on effort'. The same kanji is used in 怠ける なまける 'to be lazy', but there the okurigana is ける, so the reading is completely different. The on'yomi is たい, as in 怠慢 たいまん 'negligence'. The distractors are verbs that start with お and end in -った, so read the whole word carefully: お・こ・た・っ・た.
choice_notes: Wrong. おこった is 怒った 'got angry' or 起こった 'happened'. It is missing the た in the middle.
Wrong. おとった is 劣った, from 劣る 'to be inferior'.
Correct. おこたった = 怠った, from 怠る 'to neglect'.
Wrong. おさまった is 収まった / 治まった 'settled down, calmed down'.

vocab.meaning: to neglect, to be negligent, to fail to do
vocab.example: 毎日{まいにち}の練習{れんしゅう}を怠{おこた}ると、すぐに下手{へた}になる。
vocab.example_translation: If you neglect daily practice, you will soon get worse.

vocab.example: 車{くるま}に注意{ちゅうい}して道{みち}を渡{わた}ってください。
vocab.example_translation: Please watch out for cars when crossing the road.

vocab.example: 雪{ゆき}の日{ひ}は事故{じこ}が多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: There are many accidents on snowy days.

vocab.example: 昨日{きのう}、駅前{えきまえ}で火事{かじ}が起{お}きた。
vocab.example_translation: A fire broke out in front of the station yesterday.

vocab.meaning: to be lazy, to slack off
vocab.example: 弟{おとうと}は勉強{べんきょう}を怠{なま}けてばかりいる。
vocab.example_translation: My younger brother does nothing but slack off on his studies.

grammar.meaning: because ~, as a result of ~ (often for a bad result)
grammar.formation: Plain past / present form + ために / noun + のために
grammar.example: 寝坊{ねぼう}したために、会議{かいぎ}に遅{おく}れた。
grammar.example_translation: Because I overslept, I was late for the meeting.

grammar.meaning: to end up ~ (often with regret); to do ~ completely
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + しまう
grammar.example: 大切{たいせつ}な書類{しょるい}をなくしてしまった。
grammar.example_translation: I ended up losing an important document.

question: 売{う}り上{あ}げが伸{の}びなかったため、その会社{かいしゃ}は海外市場{かいがいしじょう}から[[撤退]]した。
translation: Because its sales did not grow, the company withdrew from the overseas market.
explanation: 撤退 is read てったい and means 'withdrawal, pulling out' (from a market, a battle, etc.). The on'yomi of 撤 is てつ, but like 圧 (あつ → あっ), てつ shrinks to てっ before a k-, s-, t- or h- sound, and a following h- sound changes to p-: 撤回 てっかい 'retraction', 撤去 てっきょ 'removal', 撤収 てっしゅう 'withdrawal, clearing out', 撤廃 てっぱい 'abolition'. 退 is read たい, as in 引退 いんたい 'retirement' and 退院 たいいん 'leaving hospital'; its kun'yomi is しりぞく (退く 'to retreat'). The funniest trap is てつだい, which is a real but totally different word: 手伝い 'help'.
choice_notes: Wrong. The small っ is missing. てつ becomes てっ before た.
Correct. てったい = 撤退 'withdrawal'.
Wrong. てつだい is 手伝い 'help, assistance'. 撤退 needs a small っ and an unvoiced た.
Wrong. 退 is read たい without a dakuten.

vocab.example: 大手{おおて}のスーパーがこの町{まち}から撤退{てったい}した。
vocab.example_translation: A major supermarket chain pulled out of this town.

vocab.example: 今月{こんげつ}の売{う}り上{あ}げは先月{せんげつ}より多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: This month's sales are higher than last month's.

vocab.meaning: to grow, to increase; to stretch, to extend
vocab.example: 子{こ}どもの身長{しんちょう}が一年{いちねん}で五{ご}センチ伸{の}びた。
vocab.example_translation: My child grew five centimeters in one year.

vocab.example: 海外{かいがい}に住{す}んだことがありますか。
vocab.example_translation: Have you ever lived abroad?

vocab.meaning: market (in the economic sense); read いちば it means a physical marketplace
vocab.example: 日本{にほん}の車{くるま}は世界{せかい}の市場{しじょう}で人気{にんき}がある。
vocab.example_translation: Japanese cars are popular in the world market.

grammar.meaning: because ~, due to ~ (formal)
grammar.formation: Plain form + ため / noun + のため
grammar.example: 台風{たいふう}のため、学校{がっこう}が休{やす}みになった。
grammar.example_translation: School was closed because of the typhoon.

question: 取引先{とりひきさき}から新{あたら}しい商品{しょうひん}のデザインを[[依頼]]された。
translation: We were asked by a client to design a new product.
explanation: 依頼 is read いらい and means 'request, commission (asking someone to do a job)'. 依 is read い, as in 依存 いぞん 'dependence'. 頼 is read らい, as in 信頼 しんらい 'trust'; its kun'yomi are たのむ (頼む 'to ask') and たよる (頼る 'to rely on'). All three distractors are real words that sound close: 異例 いれい 'exceptional', 偉い えらい 'great, important', and 偉大 いだい 'great'. Don't let familiar words pull you away from the kanji in front of you.
choice_notes: Wrong. いれい is 異例 'unprecedented, exceptional'. 頼 is read らい, not れい.
Correct. いらい = 依頼 'request, commission'.
Wrong. えらい is 偉い 'great, admirable'. 依 is read い here, not え.
Wrong. いだい is 偉大 'great, mighty'. 頼 is read らい, not だい.

vocab.example: 弁護士{べんごし}に相談{そうだん}を依頼{いらい}した。
vocab.example_translation: I asked a lawyer for a consultation.

vocab.example: 取引先{とりひきさき}に新年{しんねん}のあいさつに行{い}った。
vocab.example_translation: I went to give New Year's greetings to our clients.

vocab.example: この店{みせ}は商品{しょうひん}の種類{しゅるい}が多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: This shop has a wide variety of products.

vocab.example: このかばんはデザインがおしゃれだ。
vocab.example_translation: This bag has a stylish design.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は同僚{どうりょう}から信頼{しんらい}されている。
vocab.example_translation: He is trusted by his colleagues.

grammar.meaning: to be ~ed (by someone); the doer is marked with に or から
grammar.formation: Group 1: ない-stem + れる; Group 2: stem + られる; する → される (依頼する → 依頼される)
grammar.example: 電車{でんしゃ}の中{なか}で隣{となり}の人{ひと}に足{あし}を踏{ふ}まれた。
grammar.example_translation: On the train, my foot was stepped on by the person next to me.

question: 住民{じゅうみん}たちは、工場{こうじょう}の騒音{そうおん}がひどいと市役所{しやくしょ}に[[訴えた]]。
translation: The residents complained to city hall that the noise from the factory was terrible.
explanation: 訴えた is the past form of 訴える（うったえる）. It has several meanings: 'to complain to, to appeal to' (市役所に訴える 'complain to city hall'), 'to complain of (pain or symptoms)' (痛みを訴える), and 'to sue' (裁判所に訴える 'take to court'). The key point is the small っ: う・っ・た・え・る. The on'yomi is そ, as in 訴訟 そしょう 'lawsuit' and 起訴 きそ 'indictment'. The trap うたえた looks like 歌えた 'could sing', and うつたえた uses a big つ instead of the small っ.
choice_notes: Wrong. The small っ is missing. (うたえた would be 歌えた 'was able to sing'.)
Wrong. The つ must be a small っ: うったえた, not うつたえた.
Wrong. うたがえた is 疑えた 'was able to doubt', from 疑う. Different kanji.
Correct. うったえた = 訴えた, from 訴える 'to complain, to appeal; to sue'.

vocab.meaning: to complain (of), to appeal (to); to sue
vocab.example: 患者{かんじゃ}は頭痛{ずつう}を訴{うった}えた。
vocab.example_translation: The patient complained of a headache.

vocab.example: 住民{じゅうみん}の意見{いけん}を聞{き}いて計画{けいかく}を決{き}める。
vocab.example_translation: We will decide the plan after listening to the residents' opinions.

vocab.example: この工場{こうじょう}では車{くるま}の部品{ぶひん}を作{つく}っている。
vocab.example_translation: This factory makes car parts.

vocab.example: 夜中{よなか}の騒音{そうおん}で眠{ねむ}れなかった。
vocab.example_translation: I couldn't sleep because of the noise in the middle of the night.

vocab.example: 引{ひ}っ越{こ}したら、市役所{しやくしょ}に届{とど}けを出{だ}してください。
vocab.example_translation: After you move, please submit a notification to city hall.

vocab.example: 昨日{きのう}はひどい雨{あめ}で、外{そと}に出{で}られなかった。
vocab.example_translation: Yesterday the rain was so terrible that I couldn't go outside.

grammar.meaning: that ~ (marks the content of what is said, thought, or complained)
grammar.formation: Plain form + と + 言う / 思う / 訴える
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は明日{あした}来{く}ると言{い}った。
grammar.example_translation: He said that he would come tomorrow.

question: 会議{かいぎ}が始{はじ}まる前{まえ}に、同僚{どうりょう}と少{すこ}し[[雑談]]をした。
translation: Before the meeting started, I chatted a little with my colleagues.
explanation: 雑談 is read ざつだん and means 'small talk, idle chat'. 雑 has two on'yomi: ざつ, the common one (雑誌 ざっし 'magazine', 複雑 ふくざつ 'complicated', 混雑 こんざつ 'congestion'), and ぞう, used in a few words such as 雑巾 ぞうきん 'cleaning rag' and 雑煮 ぞうに 'New Year's soup'. 談 is read だん with a dakuten, as in 相談 そうだん 'consultation' and 冗談 じょうだん 'joke'. So the traps are: the ぞう reading of 雑, the unvoiced たん, and an extra small っ.
choice_notes: Correct. ざつだん = 雑談 'small talk, chat'.
Wrong. There is no small っ, and 談 is the voiced だん.
Wrong. ぞう is a real reading of 雑 (雑巾 ぞうきん), but 雑談 uses ざつ.
Wrong. 談 is read だん with a dakuten, not たん.

vocab.example: 休{やす}み時間{じかん}に友達{ともだち}と雑談{ざつだん}した。
vocab.example_translation: I chatted with my friends during the break.

vocab.example: 会議{かいぎ}で新{あたら}しい計画{けいかく}が決{き}まった。
vocab.example_translation: A new plan was decided at the meeting.

vocab.example: 同僚{どうりょう}と一緒{いっしょ}に昼{ひる}ご飯{はん}を食{た}べた。
vocab.example_translation: I ate lunch with a coworker.

vocab.example: 映画{えいが}は七時{しちじ}に始{はじ}まる。
vocab.example_translation: The movie starts at seven.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}はいつも冗談{じょうだん}を言{い}って人{ひと}を笑{わら}わせる。
vocab.example_translation: He always tells jokes and makes people laugh.

grammar.meaning: before ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + 前に / noun + の + 前に
grammar.example: 寝{ね}る前{まえ}に歯{は}を磨{みが}く。
grammar.example_translation: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

question: この路線{ろせん}のバスは、十五分{じゅうごふん}[[間隔]]で運行{うんこう}している。
translation: The buses on this route run at fifteen-minute intervals.
explanation: 間隔 is read かんかく and means 'interval, spacing (in time or space)': 十五分間隔 'every fifteen minutes', 一メートル間隔 'one meter apart'. 間 is read かん in on'yomi words like 時間 じかん and 期間 きかん; its kun'yomi are あいだ and ま (間に合う). 隔 is read かく, as in 隔週 かくしゅう 'every other week'; its kun'yomi is へだてる (隔てる 'to separate'). Note that 感覚 'sense, feeling' is also read かんかく (a homophone). The trap かんげき is the reading of 間隙 'gap', which uses the similar-looking kanji 隙.
choice_notes: Wrong. かんげき is 感激 'deep emotion' or 間隙 'gap'. 隙 (げき) looks like 隔, but 隔 is read かく.
Wrong. ま is a kun'yomi of 間 (間に合う), but this compound uses the on'yomi かん.
Correct. かんかく = 間隔 'interval, spacing'.
Wrong. かんがく is 漢学 'Chinese classics'. 隔 is read かく without a dakuten.

vocab.example: 木{き}を三{さん}メートル間隔{かんかく}で植{う}えた。
vocab.example_translation: We planted the trees three meters apart.

vocab.example: この路線{ろせん}は朝{あさ}とても混{こ}む。
vocab.example_translation: This line is very crowded in the morning.

vocab.example: 雪{ゆき}のため、電車{でんしゃ}の運行{うんこう}が止{と}まった。
vocab.example_translation: Train service stopped because of the snow.

vocab.meaning: sense, sensation, feeling (homophone of 間隔)
vocab.example: 寒{さむ}さで指{ゆび}の感覚{かんかく}がなくなった。
vocab.example_translation: I lost the feeling in my fingers because of the cold.

question: 彼{かれ}の説明{せつめい}は、昨日{きのう}言{い}ったことと[[矛盾]]している。
translation: His explanation contradicts what he said yesterday.
explanation: 矛盾 is read むじゅん and means 'contradiction'. It literally means 'spear and shield': in an old Chinese story, a merchant claimed his spear could pierce any shield and his shield could stop any spear, which is impossible. 矛 is read む (kun'yomi ほこ 'spear') and 盾 is read じゅん (kun'yomi たて 'shield'). In the compound, both kanji use on'yomi, so mixing in the kun'yomi ほこ is wrong. Also remember the dakuten on じゅん and the final ん.
choice_notes: Wrong. 盾 is read じゅん with a dakuten, not しゅん.
Wrong. ほこ is the kun'yomi of 矛 ('spear'), but the compound 矛盾 uses the on'yomi む.
Wrong. 盾 ends in ん: じゅん, not じゅう.
Correct. むじゅん = 矛盾 'contradiction'.

vocab.example: この記事{きじ}には矛盾{むじゅん}する点{てん}がいくつかある。
vocab.example_translation: There are several contradictory points in this article.

vocab.example: 先生{せんせい}の説明{せつめい}はとても分{わ}かりやすい。
vocab.example_translation: The teacher's explanations are very easy to understand.

vocab.example: 兵士{へいし}は盾{たて}で身{み}を守{まも}った。
vocab.example_translation: The soldier protected himself with a shield.

vocab.example: 昔{むかし}の兵士{へいし}は矛{ほこ}を持{も}って戦{たたか}った。
vocab.example_translation: Soldiers long ago fought with spears.

grammar.meaning: the thing that ~, what ~ (turns a clause into a noun)
grammar.formation: Plain form + こと (言ったこと 'what (he) said')
grammar.example: 先生{せんせい}が言{い}ったことをメモした。
grammar.example_translation: I wrote down what the teacher said.

question: 地震{じしん}に[[備えて]]、水{みず}や食料{しょくりょう}を準備{じゅんび}しておこう。
translation: Let's get water and food ready in preparation for an earthquake.
explanation: 備えて is the て-form of 備える（そなえる）'to prepare for; to be equipped with'. 〜に備えて 'in preparation for ~' is a key N2 expression. The on'yomi of 備 is び, as in 準備 じゅんび 'preparation' (in this very sentence), 設備 せつび 'facilities', and 予備 よび 'spare'. Note the homophone 供える そなえる 'to make an offering (at an altar)'. The distractors are all real verbs ending in -える with related meanings, so you must know which kanji goes with which reading.
choice_notes: Correct. そなえて = 備えて, from 備える 'to prepare for'.
Wrong. そろえて is 揃えて, from 揃える 'to gather, to arrange (a full set)'.
Wrong. たくわえて is 蓄えて, from 蓄える 'to store up, to save'.
Wrong. ととのえて is 整えて / 調えて, from 整える 'to put in order, to arrange'.

vocab.meaning: to prepare for; to be equipped with
vocab.example: 試験{しけん}に備{そな}えて、毎晩{まいばん}勉強{べんきょう}している。
vocab.example_translation: I am studying every night to prepare for the exam.

vocab.example: 日本{にほん}は地震{じしん}が多{おお}い国{くに}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Japan is a country with many earthquakes.

vocab.example: 一週間分{いっしゅうかんぶん}の食料{しょくりょう}を買{か}った。
vocab.example_translation: I bought a week's worth of food.

vocab.example: 旅行{りょこう}の準備{じゅんび}はもうできた。
vocab.example_translation: The preparations for the trip are already done.

vocab.meaning: to store up, to save (money, energy)
vocab.example: 老後{ろうご}のためにお金{かね}を蓄{たくわ}える。
vocab.example_translation: To save money for one's old age.

grammar.meaning: in preparation for ~
grammar.formation: Noun + に備えて
grammar.example: 台風{たいふう}に備{そな}えて、窓{まど}を補強{ほきょう}した。
grammar.example_translation: We reinforced the windows in preparation for the typhoon.

grammar.meaning: to do ~ in advance (for later)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + おく
grammar.example: 客{きゃく}が来{く}る前{まえ}に、部屋{へや}を掃除{そうじ}しておく。
grammar.example_translation: I will clean the room before the guests come.

grammar.meaning: let's ~ (casual); I think I'll ~
grammar.formation: Group 1: change the final う-sound to お + う (行く → 行こう); Group 2: stem + よう; する → しよう; くる → こよう
grammar.example: 一緒{いっしょ}に帰{かえ}ろう。
grammar.example_translation: Let's go home together.

question: 彼女{かのじょ}は本番{ほんばん}で実力{じつりょく}を十分{じゅうぶん}に[[発揮]]した。
translation: She fully showed her true ability in the actual performance.
explanation: 発揮 is read はっき and means 'showing, displaying (one's ability or power)'. 実力を発揮する 'to show one's real ability' and 能力を発揮する are set phrases. 発 is read はつ, and it shrinks to はっ before k-, s-, t- or h- sounds (a following h-sound also turns into p): 発見 はっけん, 発送 はっそう, 発展 はってん, 発表 はっぴょう. 発 also has a rarer reading ほつ / ほっ, as in 発作 ほっさ 'fit, attack' and 発足 ほっそく 'launch', which is where the trap ほっき comes from. 揮 is read き, as in 指揮 しき 'conducting, command'.
choice_notes: Wrong. The small っ is missing. はつ becomes はっ before き.
Correct. はっき = 発揮 'display (of ability)'.
Wrong. ほっき is 発起 'proposing, initiating'. 発 can be ほっ in some words, but 発揮 uses はっ.
Wrong. 揮 is read き without a dakuten.

vocab.meaning: display, exhibition (of one's ability or power)
vocab.example: 新{あたら}しい環境{かんきょう}で能力{のうりょく}を発揮{はっき}したい。
vocab.example_translation: I want to show my abilities in a new environment.

vocab.meaning: the real thing, the actual performance (not a rehearsal)
vocab.example: 練習{れんしゅう}ではうまくできたのに、本番{ほんばん}で失敗{しっぱい}した。
vocab.example_translation: I did well in practice, but I failed in the real performance.

vocab.example: 試験{しけん}で自分{じぶん}の実力{じつりょく}を試{ため}したい。
vocab.example_translation: I want to test my real ability in the exam.

vocab.meaning: enough, sufficient; fully (read じゅっぷん, it means 'ten minutes')
vocab.example: 時間{じかん}は十分{じゅうぶん}にあるから、急{いそ}がなくていい。
vocab.example_translation: There is plenty of time, so you don't need to hurry.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}はオーケストラの指揮{しき}をしている。
vocab.example_translation: He conducts an orchestra.

question: この作家{さっか}の文章{ぶんしょう}は[[抽象的]]で、理解{りかい}するのが難{むずか}しい。
translation: This author's writing is abstract and hard to understand.
explanation: 抽象的 is read ちゅうしょうてき and means 'abstract'; its opposite is 具体的 ぐたいてき 'concrete'. 抽 is read ちゅう, as in 抽選 ちゅうせん 'lottery' and 抽出 ちゅうしゅつ 'extraction'. 象 has two on'yomi: しょう, used in 抽象, 印象 いんしょう 'impression', 現象 げんしょう 'phenomenon', and 対象 たいしょう 'target'; and ぞう, used in 象 ぞう 'elephant'. That second reading is the trap ちゅうぞうてき. Be careful not to confuse 象 with 像 (ぞう, as in 想像 そうぞう 'imagination'). The suffix 的 (てき) turns a noun into a な-adjective: 抽象的な, 具体的な.
choice_notes: Wrong. ぞう is a real reading of 象 (象 ぞう 'elephant'), but 抽象 uses しょう.
Wrong. 抽 is read ちゅう, not ちょう. (ちょうしょう is 嘲笑 'ridicule'.)
Correct. ちゅうしょうてき = 抽象的 'abstract'.
Wrong. 象 is read しょう without a dakuten here.

vocab.example: 抽象的{ちゅうしょうてき}な説明{せつめい}ではなく、例{れい}を挙{あ}げてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please give an example instead of an abstract explanation.

vocab.example: 好{す}きな作家{さっか}の新{あたら}しい小説{しょうせつ}が出{で}た。
vocab.example_translation: A new novel by my favorite author came out.

vocab.example: 短{みじか}くて分{わ}かりやすい文章{ぶんしょう}を書{か}きたい。
vocab.example_translation: I want to write short, easy-to-understand texts.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}の気持{きも}ちが理解{りかい}できない。
vocab.example_translation: I can't understand his feelings.

vocab.example: もっと具体的{ぐたいてき}に話{はな}してください。
vocab.example_translation: Please speak more specifically.

grammar.meaning: doing ~ is (hard / easy / fun ...) (の turns a verb into a noun)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + のが + 難しい・好きだ・苦手だ etc.
grammar.example: 朝{あさ}早{はや}く起{お}きるのが苦手{にがて}だ。
grammar.example_translation: I am bad at getting up early in the morning.

grammar.meaning: ~ and (also a light reason: 'is ~, so ...')
grammar.formation: な-adjective / noun + で
grammar.example: この部屋{へや}は静{しず}かで、勉強{べんきょう}しやすい。
grammar.example_translation: This room is quiet and easy to study in.

question: 彼{かれ}はいつも[[鋭い]]質問{しつもん}をして、先生{せんせい}を困{こま}らせる。
translation: He always asks sharp questions and puts the teacher on the spot.
explanation: 鋭い is read するどい and means 'sharp, keen': 鋭い質問 'a sharp question', 鋭いナイフ 'a sharp knife', 勘が鋭い 'to have sharp intuition'. Its on'yomi is えい, as in 鋭角 えいかく 'acute angle'. The opposite is 鈍い にぶい 'dull', which has the same metal radical 金 on the left, so the two kanji are easy to mix up. Also remember that the ど has a dakuten.
choice_notes: Correct. するどい = 鋭い 'sharp, keen'.
Wrong. The dakuten is missing: it is ど, not と.
Wrong. ずるい means 'sly, unfair'. It sounds a little similar, but it is a different word.
Wrong. にぶい is the reading of 鈍い 'dull', the opposite word. 鈍 also has the 金 radical, so do not confuse the two kanji.

vocab.example: 猫{ねこ}は鋭{するど}い爪{つめ}を持{も}っている。
vocab.example_translation: Cats have sharp claws.

vocab.example: 何{なに}か質問{しつもん}はありますか。
vocab.example_translation: Do you have any questions?

vocab.meaning: to be troubled, to be at a loss
vocab.example: 財布{さいふ}をなくして困{こま}っている。
vocab.example_translation: I lost my wallet and I am in trouble.

vocab.example: 年{とし}を取{と}ると反応{はんのう}が鈍{にぶ}くなる。
vocab.example_translation: As you get older, your reactions become slower.

grammar.meaning: to make someone ~ / to cause someone to feel ~ (困らせる 'to trouble someone')
grammar.formation: Group 1: ない-stem + せる (困る → 困らせる); Group 2: stem + させる; する → させる
grammar.example: 子{こ}どもを泣{な}かせてはいけない。
grammar.example_translation: You must not make the child cry.

question: 台風{たいふう}によって、農作物{のうさくもつ}に大{おお}きな[[損害]]が出{で}た。
translation: The typhoon caused great damage to the crops.
explanation: 損害 is read そんがい and means 'damage, loss'. 損 is read そん, as in 損失 そんしつ 'loss' and 損得 そんとく 'profit and loss'; its kun'yomi is そこなう (損なう 'to harm'). 害 is read がい with a dakuten, as in 被害 ひがい 'damage (suffered)', 災害 さいがい 'disaster', and 公害 こうがい 'pollution'. The traps: そんかい is a real word 損壊 'destruction (of buildings)' that uses a different second kanji, ぞんがい is 存外 'unexpectedly', and そう is simply not a reading of 損.
choice_notes: Wrong. そんかい is 損壊 'destruction (of buildings)', written with 壊. 害 is read がい with a dakuten.
Wrong. ぞんがい is 存外 'unexpectedly'. 損 is read そん without a dakuten.
Wrong. 損 is read そん (ending in ん), not そう.
Correct. そんがい = 損害 'damage, loss'.

vocab.example: 事故{じこ}の損害{そんがい}は保険{ほけん}で補償{ほしょう}された。
vocab.example_translation: The damage from the accident was covered by insurance.

vocab.example: 台風{たいふう}が近{ちか}づいている。
vocab.example_translation: A typhoon is approaching.

vocab.example: 雨{あめ}が少{すく}なくて農作物{のうさくもつ}がよく育{そだ}たない。
vocab.example_translation: There is little rain, so the crops are not growing well.

vocab.example: 地震{じしん}で多{おお}くの家{いえ}が被害{ひがい}を受{う}けた。
vocab.example_translation: Many houses were damaged in the earthquake.

grammar.meaning: due to ~, because of ~ (formal)
grammar.formation: Noun + によって
grammar.example: 大雨{おおあめ}によって、川{かわ}の水{みず}が増{ふ}えた。
grammar.example_translation: The river rose because of the heavy rain.

question: 日本{にほん}は多{おお}くの国{くに}と[[貿易]]を行{おこな}っている。
translation: Japan carries out trade with many countries.
explanation: 貿易 is read ぼうえき and means 'trade (between countries)'. 貿 is read ぼう with a dakuten and a long vowel; it appears almost only in this word. 易 has two on'yomi with different meanings: えき 'exchange' (貿易, 交易 こうえき) and い 'easy' (容易 ようい 'easy', 安易 あんい 'too easy, facile', 簡易 かんい 'simple'). Its kun'yomi is やさしい (易しい 'easy'). In 貿易 it is えき, so ぼうい is the 'other reading of the same kanji' trap.
choice_notes: Wrong. い is a real reading of 易 (容易 ようい 'easy'), but 貿易 uses えき.
Wrong. 貿 is read ぼう with a dakuten, not ほう.
Correct. ぼうえき = 貿易 'trade'.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 貿 is ぼう, not ぼ.

vocab.example: 父{ちち}は貿易会社{ぼうえきがいしゃ}で働{はたら}いている。
vocab.example_translation: My father works for a trading company.

vocab.meaning: to do, to carry out, to hold (formal)
vocab.example: 来月{らいげつ}、学校{がっこう}で運動会{うんどうかい}が行{おこな}われる。
vocab.example_translation: A sports day will be held at school next month.

vocab.example: この問題{もんだい}を解決{かいけつ}するのは容易{ようい}ではない。
vocab.example_translation: Solving this problem is not easy.

vocab.example: この本{ほん}は易{やさ}しい日本語{にほんご}で書{か}かれている。
vocab.example_translation: This book is written in easy Japanese.

question: 彼{かれ}は[[貧しい]]家庭{かてい}に生{う}まれたが、努力{どりょく}して医者{いしゃ}になった。
translation: He was born into a poor family, but he worked hard and became a doctor.
explanation: 貧しい is read まずしい and means 'poor (having little money)'. The on'yomi of 貧 is ひん (貧困 ひんこん 'poverty', 貧富 ひんぷ 'rich and poor') and びん (貧乏 びんぼう 'poor', a very common casual word). The trap とぼしい is the reading of 乏しい 'scarce, lacking', and its kanji 乏 is the second kanji of 貧乏, so the two words are related in meaning. まぶしい 'dazzling' only sounds similar. Also keep the dakuten on ず.
choice_notes: Wrong. まぶしい is 眩しい 'dazzling, too bright'. It only sounds similar.
Correct. まずしい = 貧しい 'poor'.
Wrong. The dakuten is missing: it is ず, not す.
Wrong. とぼしい is 乏しい 'scarce, lacking'. Its kanji 乏 appears in 貧乏 びんぼう, but 貧しい is まずしい.

vocab.example: 昔{むかし}、この村{むら}の人々{ひとびと}は貧{まず}しい生活{せいかつ}をしていた。
vocab.example_translation: Long ago, the people of this village lived poor lives.

vocab.example: 彼女{かのじょ}は仕事{しごと}より家庭{かてい}を大切{たいせつ}にしている。
vocab.example_translation: She values her family more than her work.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}は東京{とうきょう}で生{う}まれた。
vocab.example_translation: I was born in Tokyo.

vocab.example: 毎日{まいにち}の努力{どりょく}が大切{たいせつ}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Daily effort is important.

vocab.example: この国{くに}は資源{しげん}が乏{とぼ}しい。
vocab.example_translation: This country is poor in natural resources.

question: 母{はは}は仕事{しごと}を辞{や}めて、祖父{そふ}の[[介護]]をしている。
translation: My mother quit her job and is taking care of my grandfather.
explanation: 介護 is read かいご and means 'nursing care (for elderly or disabled people)'. 介 is read かい, as in 紹介 しょうかい 'introduction' and 介入 かいにゅう 'intervention'. 護 is read ご with a dakuten, as in 保護 ほご 'protection', 看護 かんご 'nursing', and 弁護士 べんごし 'lawyer'. The most dangerous trap is かいこ, which is the real word 解雇 'dismissal, firing (from a job)'. In this sentence, which is also about work, it could easily mislead you.
choice_notes: Wrong. かいこ is 解雇 'dismissal (from a job)' or 蚕 'silkworm'. 護 is read ご with a dakuten.
Wrong. 介 is read かい without a dakuten. がい is the reading of 外 (外国 がいこく).
Wrong. かいごう is 会合 'meeting, gathering'. 護 is a short ご.
Correct. かいご = 介護 'nursing care'.

vocab.meaning: nursing care (of the elderly or disabled)
vocab.example: 介護{かいご}の仕事{しごと}は体力{たいりょく}が必要{ひつよう}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Care work requires physical strength.

vocab.meaning: to quit, to resign (a job, school)
vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は先月{せんげつ}会社{かいしゃ}を辞{や}めた。
vocab.example_translation: He quit his company last month.

vocab.example: 祖父{そふ}は毎朝{まいあさ}散歩{さんぽ}をする。
vocab.example_translation: My grandfather takes a walk every morning.

vocab.meaning: nursing (medical care of the sick or injured)
vocab.example: 姉{あね}は病院{びょういん}で看護師{かんごし}として働{はたら}いている。
vocab.example_translation: My older sister works as a nurse at a hospital.

question: スマートフォンの[[普及]]により、人々{ひとびと}の生活{せいかつ}は大{おお}きく変{か}わった。
translation: With the spread of smartphones, people's lives have changed greatly.
explanation: 普及 is read ふきゅう and means 'spread, popularization (of a product, idea, technology)'. 普 is read ふ, as in 普通 ふつう 'normal' and 普段 ふだん 'usually'. 及 is read きゅう, as in 言及 げんきゅう 'mention'; its kun'yomi is およぶ (及ぶ 'to reach, to extend'). The distractors are real words with similar sounds: 復旧 ふっきゅう 'restoration (of service)', 不況 ふきょう 'recession'. Remember: no small っ, and 及 is きゅう, not きょう.
choice_notes: Correct. ふきゅう = 普及 'spread, popularization'.
Wrong. ふっきゅう is 復旧 'restoration, recovery (of trains, power)'. 普及 has no small っ.
Wrong. ふきょう is 不況 'recession'. 及 is read きゅう, not きょう.
Wrong. 普 is read ふ without a dakuten.

vocab.example: インターネットの普及{ふきゅう}で、買{か}い物{もの}の方法{ほうほう}が変{か}わった。
vocab.example_translation: With the spread of the internet, the way we shop has changed.

vocab.example: 町{まち}の人々{ひとびと}が祭{まつ}りを楽{たの}しんだ。
vocab.example_translation: The people of the town enjoyed the festival.

vocab.example: 都会{とかい}の生活{せいかつ}にもう慣{な}れた。
vocab.example_translation: I have already gotten used to city life.

vocab.example: 引{ひ}っ越{こ}してから、生活{せいかつ}のリズムが変{か}わった。
vocab.example_translation: My daily rhythm changed after I moved.

vocab.meaning: to reach, to extend, to amount to
vocab.example: 会議{かいぎ}は五時間{ごじかん}に及{およ}んだ。
vocab.example_translation: The meeting lasted as long as five hours.

grammar.meaning: due to ~, as a result of ~ (により is the more formal, written form)
grammar.formation: Noun + により / によって
grammar.example: 法律{ほうりつ}の改正{かいせい}により、税金{ぜいきん}が上{あ}がった。
grammar.example_translation: Taxes went up due to the revision of the law.

question: 二{ふた}つの絵{え}はよく似{に}ているが、色{いろ}が[[微妙]]に違{ちが}う。
translation: The two paintings look very alike, but their colors are subtly different.
explanation: 微妙 is read びみょう and means 'subtle, delicate'. In casual speech it also means 'doubtful, iffy, not great' (その服、ちょっと微妙 'that outfit is kind of meh'). 微 is read び with a dakuten, as in 微笑 びしょう 'smile' and 微生物 びせいぶつ 'microorganism'; it also appears in 微笑む ほほえむ 'to smile', which is a special reading of the whole word. 妙 is read みょう, as in 奇妙 きみょう 'strange'. Watch out for the similar-looking kanji 徴 (ちょう, as in 特徴 とくちょう 'feature'): 微 and 徴 differ only in the middle part. Also keep the long vowel みょう.
choice_notes: Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 妙 is みょう, not みょ.
Correct. びみょう = 微妙 'subtle'.
Wrong. ちょう is the reading of the similar-looking kanji 徴 (特徴 とくちょう), not 微.
Wrong. 微 is read び with a dakuten, not ひ.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}が来{く}るかどうかは微妙{びみょう}だ。
vocab.example_translation: It is doubtful whether he will come.

vocab.example: 娘{むすめ}は母親{ははおや}によく似{に}ている。
vocab.example_translation: The daughter looks a lot like her mother.

vocab.meaning: to differ, to be different; to be wrong
vocab.example: 私{わたし}の意見{いけん}は彼{かれ}と少{すこ}し違{ちが}う。
vocab.example_translation: My opinion is a little different from his.

vocab.example: この町{まち}の特徴{とくちょう}は古{ふる}い建物{たてもの}が多{おお}いことだ。
vocab.example_translation: A feature of this town is that it has many old buildings.

grammar.meaning: to look like ~, to resemble ~ (似る is almost always used as 似ている)
grammar.formation: Noun + に似ている
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}の声{こえ}は父親{ちちおや}に似{に}ている。
grammar.example_translation: His voice is like his father's.

question: 頂上{ちょうじょう}までの道{みち}は[[険しく]]、何度{なんど}も休{やす}みながら登{のぼ}った。
translation: The path to the summit was steep, so we climbed while taking many breaks.
explanation: 険しく is the connective form of 険しい（けわしい）'steep, rugged; stern (expression)': 険しい山道 'a steep mountain path', 険しい表情 'a stern look'. The on'yomi of 険 is けん, as in 危険 きけん 'danger', 冒険 ぼうけん 'adventure', and 保険 ほけん 'insurance'. Similar-looking kanji with the same right side are also read けん: 検 (検査 けんさ), 験 (試験 しけん), 倹 (倹約 けんやく). The distractors are all real -しい adjectives: 厳しい きびしい 'strict' is especially tempting because 'a harsh path' sounds possible.
choice_notes: Wrong. きびしく is 厳しく, from 厳しい 'strict, severe'. Different kanji.
Wrong. くわしく is 詳しく, from 詳しい 'detailed'. Different kanji.
Correct. けわしく = 険しく, from 険しい 'steep, rugged'.
Wrong. はげしく is 激しく, from 激しい 'violent, intense'. Different kanji.

vocab.example: 父{ちち}は険{けわ}しい顔{かお}で話{はなし}を聞{き}いていた。
vocab.example_translation: My father listened with a stern face.

vocab.example: 富士山{ふじさん}の頂上{ちょうじょう}から日{ひ}の出{で}を見{み}た。
vocab.example_translation: I watched the sunrise from the summit of Mt. Fuji.

vocab.example: 何度{なんど}も電話{でんわ}したが、つながらなかった。
vocab.example_translation: I called many times, but couldn't get through.

vocab.example: 毎年{まいとし}、家族{かぞく}で山{やま}に登{のぼ}る。
vocab.example_translation: Every year my family climbs a mountain.

vocab.example: この川{かわ}で泳{およ}ぐのは危険{きけん}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Swimming in this river is dangerous.

grammar.meaning: while ~ (two actions by the same person at the same time)
grammar.formation: Verb masu-stem + ながら
grammar.example: 音楽{おんがく}を聞{き}きながら勉強{べんきょう}する。
grammar.example_translation: I study while listening to music.

grammar.meaning: ~ and ... (joins clauses in written style; also a light reason)
grammar.formation: い-adjective without い + く、 (険しい → 険しく、)
grammar.example: 部屋{へや}は狭{せま}く、窓{まど}も小{ちい}さい。
grammar.example_translation: The room is small, and the windows are small too.

question: 交差点{こうさてん}でトラックと乗用車{じょうようしゃ}が[[衝突]]した。
translation: A truck and a passenger car collided at the intersection.
explanation: 衝突 is read しょうとつ and means 'collision, crash'; it is also used for opinions: 意見が衝突する 'opinions clash'. 衝 is read しょう, as in 衝撃 しょうげき 'shock' and 衝動 しょうどう 'impulse'. 突 is read とつ, as in 突然 とつぜん 'suddenly'; it becomes とっ in 突破 とっぱ 'breakthrough'. Its kun'yomi is つく (突く 'to poke'). All three distractors change one small detail: a dakuten on と, a missing long vowel, or a dakuten on しょう. Read each sound carefully: しょ・う・と・つ.
choice_notes: Correct. しょうとつ = 衝突 'collision'.
Wrong. 突 is read とつ without a dakuten.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 衝 is しょう, not しょ.
Wrong. 衝 is read しょう without a dakuten.

vocab.example: 会議{かいぎ}で二人{ふたり}の意見{いけん}が衝突{しょうとつ}した。
vocab.example_translation: The two people's opinions clashed at the meeting.

vocab.example: 次{つぎ}の交差点{こうさてん}を右{みぎ}に曲{ま}がってください。
vocab.example_translation: Please turn right at the next intersection.

vocab.example: 駐車場{ちゅうしゃじょう}に乗用車{じょうようしゃ}が十台{じゅうだい}止{と}まっている。
vocab.example_translation: Ten passenger cars are parked in the parking lot.

vocab.example: 大{おお}きなトラックが家{いえ}の前{まえ}を通{とお}った。
vocab.example_translation: A big truck passed in front of the house.

vocab.example: 突然{とつぜん}、雨{あめ}が降{ふ}り出{だ}した。
vocab.example_translation: Suddenly it started to rain.

question: 話{はな}し合{あ}いの結果{けっか}、両者{りょうしゃ}はお互{たが}いに[[妥協]]することにした。
translation: As a result of the discussion, both sides decided to compromise with each other.
explanation: 妥協 is read だきょう and means 'compromise'. 妥 is read だ with a dakuten, as in 妥当 だとう 'appropriate, reasonable'. 協 is read きょう, as in 協力 きょうりょく 'cooperation' and 協会 きょうかい 'association'. The traps: removing the dakuten (たきょう), dropping the long vowel (だきょ), and adding a small っ (だっきょう). An extra tip: 妥協しない means 'to make no compromises', often used about quality (品質に妥協しない).
choice_notes: Wrong. 妥 is read だ with a dakuten, not た.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 協 is きょう, not きょ.
Wrong. There is no small っ in 妥協.
Correct. だきょう = 妥協 'compromise'.

vocab.example: 品質{ひんしつ}については一切{いっさい}妥協{だきょう}しない。
vocab.example_translation: We make no compromises at all on quality.

vocab.example: クラスで話{はな}し合{あ}いをして、旅行{りょこう}の行{い}き先{さき}を決{き}めた。
vocab.example_translation: We discussed it as a class and decided where to go on the trip.

vocab.example: テストの結果{けっか}が出{で}た。
vocab.example_translation: The test results came out.

vocab.example: 両者{りょうしゃ}の意見{いけん}をよく聞{き}いてから判断{はんだん}する。
vocab.example_translation: I will decide after listening carefully to both sides.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}たちはお互{たが}いに助{たす}け合{あ}っている。
vocab.example_translation: We help each other.

grammar.meaning: as a result of ~
grammar.formation: Noun + の結果 / Verb た-form + 結果
grammar.example: 調査{ちょうさ}の結果{けっか}、原因{げんいん}が分{わ}かった。
grammar.example_translation: As a result of the investigation, the cause became clear.

grammar.meaning: to decide to ~ (one's own decision)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない form + ことにする
grammar.example: 来年{らいねん}から毎日{まいにち}運動{うんどう}することにした。
grammar.example_translation: I decided to exercise every day starting next year.

question: 父{ちち}は三十年間{さんじゅうねんかん}、教育{きょういく}の仕事{しごと}に[[携わって]]きた。
translation: My father has been involved in education work for thirty years.
explanation: 携わって is the て-form of 携わる（たずさわる）'to be engaged in, to work in (a field)'. It is used with に: 教育に携わる 'to work in education', 医療に携わる 'to work in medicine'. The same kanji also makes 携える たずさえる 'to carry (something) with you', which is the trap たずさえて. Look at the okurigana: わる → たずさわる, える → たずさえる. The on'yomi of 携 is けい, as in 携帯 けいたい 'carrying; mobile phone' and 提携 ていけい 'partnership'. かかわる 'to be involved' has a similar meaning but is written 関わる.
choice_notes: Wrong. たずさえて is 携えて, from 携える 'to carry with one'. Same kanji, but the okurigana is える, not わる.
Correct. たずさわって = 携わって, from 携わる 'to be engaged in'.
Wrong. かかわって is 関わって, from 関わる 'to be involved in'. Similar meaning, different kanji.
Wrong. さわって is 触って, from 触る 'to touch'. Different kanji.

vocab.meaning: to be engaged in, to take part in, to work in (a field)
vocab.example: 将来{しょうらい}は医療{いりょう}に携{たずさ}わる仕事{しごと}がしたい。
vocab.example_translation: In the future I want a job in the medical field.

vocab.example: 子{こ}どもの教育{きょういく}にはお金{かね}がかかる。
vocab.example_translation: Educating children costs money.

vocab.meaning: for ~ years, a period of ~ years
vocab.example: 私{わたし}は三年間{さんねんかん}日本{にほん}に住{す}んでいた。
vocab.example_translation: I lived in Japan for three years.

vocab.meaning: carrying (with you); mobile phone (short for 携帯電話)
vocab.example: 外出{がいしゅつ}するときは必{かなら}ず携帯{けいたい}を持{も}っていく。
vocab.example_translation: I always take my mobile phone when I go out.

vocab.meaning: to be involved in, to be related to
vocab.example: これは命{いのち}に関{かか}わる問題{もんだい}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This is a matter of life and death.

grammar.meaning: have been ~ing (an action continuing from the past up to the present)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + くる
grammar.example: この店{みせ}は百年前{ひゃくねんまえ}から同{おな}じ味{あじ}を守{まも}ってきた。
grammar.example_translation: This shop has kept the same taste for a hundred years.

question: 地震{じしん}が起{お}きたときこそ、[[冷静]]に行動{こうどう}することが大切{たいせつ}だ。
translation: It is precisely when an earthquake happens that it is important to act calmly.
explanation: 冷静 is read れいせい and means 'calm, composed, cool-headed'. 冷 is read れい, as in 冷蔵庫 れいぞうこ 'refrigerator' and 冷房 れいぼう 'air conditioning'; its kun'yomi include つめたい (冷たい), ひえる (冷える), and さめる (冷める). 静 is usually read せい, as in 安静 あんせい 'rest' and 静止 せいし 'standstill'; its kun'yomi is しずか (静か). 静 has a rare second on'yomi じょう (静脈 じょうみゃく 'vein'), which is the trap れいじょう. Also, 静 is never voiced to ぜい.
choice_notes: Wrong. じょう is a rare reading of 静 (静脈 じょうみゃく), and れいじょう is 礼状 'thank-you letter' or 令嬢 'young lady'. 冷静 uses せい.
Wrong. 静 is read せい without a dakuten.
Correct. れいせい = 冷静 'calm, composed'.
Wrong. 冷 is read れい, so the い is missing.

vocab.example: 彼女{かのじょ}はどんなときでも冷静{れいせい}だ。
vocab.example_translation: She is calm no matter what happens.

vocab.example: 昨夜{さくや}、小{ちい}さな地震{じしん}があった。
vocab.example_translation: There was a small earthquake last night.

vocab.example: 言葉{ことば}より行動{こうどう}で示{しめ}してほしい。
vocab.example_translation: I want you to show it with actions rather than words.

vocab.example: 家族{かぞく}は私{わたし}にとって一番{いちばん}大切{たいせつ}なものだ。
vocab.example_translation: My family is the most important thing to me.

vocab.meaning: to happen, to occur (also: to get up)
vocab.example: どこで事故{じこ}が起{お}きたか教{おし}えてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please tell me where the accident happened.

grammar.meaning: precisely ~, ~ indeed (strong emphasis on the word before it)
grammar.formation: Noun / 〜とき / 〜から + こそ
grammar.example: 今度{こんど}こそ試験{しけん}に合格{ごうかく}したい。
grammar.example_translation: This time for sure, I want to pass the exam.

grammar.meaning: it is important to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことが大切だ
grammar.example: 毎日{まいにち}少{すこ}しずつ続{つづ}けることが大切{たいせつ}だ。
grammar.example_translation: It is important to keep at it a little every day.

question: 社会{しゃかい}の[[秩序]]を守{まも}るために、法律{ほうりつ}がある。
translation: Laws exist in order to maintain social order.
explanation: 秩序 is read ちつじょ and means 'order (in society, in a group)': 社会の秩序 'social order', 秩序を守る 'to keep order'. 秩 is read ちつ and appears almost only in this word. 序 is read じょ with a SHORT vowel, as in 順序 じゅんじょ 'order, sequence' and 序盤 じょばん 'early stage'. The traps: adding a long vowel (じょう), adding a small っ (a small っ is never used before じ in words like this), and てつ, which is the reading of 鉄 (てつ 'iron'). 鉄 and 秩 share the same right-hand part 失, so they look alike.
choice_notes: Wrong. 序 is a short じょ, not じょう.
Wrong. There is no small っ. 秩 keeps its full reading ちつ.
Wrong. てつ is the reading of 鉄 'iron', which shares the part 失 with 秩. 秩 is read ちつ.
Correct. ちつじょ = 秩序 'order'.

vocab.example: 災害{さいがい}のあとでも、人々{ひとびと}は秩序{ちつじょ}を保{たも}って行動{こうどう}した。
vocab.example_translation: Even after the disaster, people acted in an orderly way.

vocab.example: 社会{しゃかい}に出{で}ると、責任{せきにん}が重{おも}くなる。
vocab.example_translation: Once you go out into the working world, your responsibilities become heavier.

vocab.meaning: to protect; to keep (a rule, a promise)
vocab.example: 交通{こうつう}ルールを守{まも}りましょう。
vocab.example_translation: Let's follow the traffic rules.

vocab.example: 法律{ほうりつ}を守{まも}るのは国民{こくみん}の義務{ぎむ}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Obeying the law is a citizen's duty.

vocab.example: 順序{じゅんじょ}よく説明{せつめい}してください。
vocab.example_translation: Please explain things in the proper order.

grammar.meaning: in order to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ために / noun + のために
grammar.example: 日本語{にほんご}を勉強{べんきょう}するために日本{にほん}に来{き}た。
grammar.example_translation: I came to Japan in order to study Japanese.

question: 最近{さいきん}の若者{わかもの}は、車{くるま}を買{か}わない[[傾向]]がある。
translation: Young people these days tend not to buy cars.
explanation: 傾向 is read けいこう and means 'tendency, trend'. 〜傾向がある / 〜傾向にある 'there is a tendency to ~' is a very common written expression. 傾 is read けい, as in 傾斜 けいしゃ 'slope'; its kun'yomi is かたむく (傾く 'to lean, to tilt'). 向 is read こう, as in 方向 ほうこう 'direction' and 意向 いこう 'intention'; its kun'yomi is むく (向く 'to face'). The traps are real words that sound almost the same: 敬語 けいご 'honorific language' and 稽古 けいこ 'practice, lesson'. Both end in a short vowel, but 向 is a long こう.
choice_notes: Wrong. けいご is 敬語 'honorific language'. 向 is こう, not ご.
Correct. けいこう = 傾向 'tendency'.
Wrong. 傾 is read けい, so the い is missing.
Wrong. けいこ is 稽古 'practice, lesson'. 向 needs the long vowel こう.

vocab.example: 日本{にほん}では子{こ}どもの数{かず}が減{へ}る傾向{けいこう}にある。
vocab.example_translation: In Japan, the number of children is on a downward trend.

vocab.example: 最近{さいきん}、駅前{えきまえ}に新{あたら}しいカフェができた。
vocab.example_translation: A new café opened in front of the station recently.

vocab.example: この町{まち}は若者{わかもの}に人気{にんき}がある。
vocab.example_translation: This town is popular with young people.

vocab.meaning: to lean, to tilt, to incline
vocab.example: 地震{じしん}で家{いえ}が少{すこ}し傾{かたむ}いた。
vocab.example_translation: The house tilted a little because of the earthquake.

grammar.meaning: to tend to ~, there is a tendency to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない form + 傾向がある; noun + の + 傾向がある
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は何{なん}でも一人{ひとり}で決{き}める傾向{けいこう}がある。
grammar.example_translation: He tends to decide everything by himself.

question: お気{き}に入{い}りのセーターを洗濯機{せんたくき}で洗{あら}ったら、[[縮んで]]しまった。
translation: When I washed my favorite sweater in the washing machine, it shrank.
explanation: 縮んで is the て-form of 縮む（ちぢむ）'to shrink'. Related verbs: 縮める ちぢめる 'to shorten, to make smaller' and 縮まる ちぢまる 'to become shorter (a gap, a distance)'. The on'yomi is しゅく, as in 縮小 しゅくしょう 'reduction' and 短縮 たんしゅく 'shortening'. The big trap is the kana spelling: when the same sound repeats and the second one becomes voiced, Japanese writes ぢ or づ, not じ or ず: ちぢむ, つづく (続く). So ちじむ is a spelling mistake. The other distractors are real verbs with related meanings: しぼむ 'to wither, to deflate' and いたむ 'to be damaged'.
choice_notes: Wrong. The spelling must be ちぢ (ち + voiced ち = ぢ), not ちじ.
Wrong. しぼんで is 萎んで, from 萎む 'to wither, to deflate (like a balloon)'.
Correct. ちぢんで = 縮んで, from 縮む 'to shrink'.
Wrong. いたんで is 傷んで, from 傷む 'to get damaged, to go bad'. Different kanji.

vocab.example: 年{とし}を取{と}ると背{せ}が縮{ちぢ}むと言{い}われている。
vocab.example_translation: It is said that people get shorter as they age.

vocab.example: これは私{わたし}のお気{き}に入{い}りの店{みせ}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This is my favorite shop.

vocab.example: 新{あたら}しい洗濯機{せんたくき}は音{おと}が静{しず}かだ。
vocab.example_translation: The new washing machine is quiet.

vocab.example: 寒{さむ}いのでセーターを着{き}た。
vocab.example_translation: It was cold, so I put on a sweater.

vocab.meaning: to shorten, to reduce, to shrink (something)
vocab.example: 練習{れんしゅう}して、タイムを一秒{いちびょう}縮{ちぢ}めた。
vocab.example_translation: By practicing, I cut my time by one second.

grammar.meaning: when I did ~, (I found that) ...
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + ら
grammar.example: 窓{まど}を開{あ}けたら、雪{ゆき}が降{ふ}っていた。
grammar.example_translation: When I opened the window, it was snowing.

grammar.meaning: to end up ~ (with regret or surprise)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + しまう (〜んでしまう after む / ぶ / ぬ verbs)
grammar.example: 電車{でんしゃ}に傘{かさ}を忘{わす}れてしまった。
grammar.example_translation: I left my umbrella on the train.

question: 父{ちち}は来月{らいげつ}から、病院{びょういん}で目{め}の[[治療]]を受{う}けることになった。
translation: It has been decided that my father will receive eye treatment at the hospital starting next month.
explanation: 治療 is read ちりょう and means 'medical treatment'. 治 has two on'yomi: ち, as in 治療 and 治安 ちあん 'public safety', and じ, as in 政治 せいじ 'politics' and 退治 たいじ 'getting rid of'. Its kun'yomi are なおる / なおす (治る 'to get better', 治す 'to cure') and おさめる (治める 'to govern'). 療 is read りょう, as in 医療 いりょう 'medical care' and 療養 りょうよう 'recuperation'. So the main trap is the じ reading of 治; the others drop the long vowel or change りょう to りゅう.
choice_notes: Correct. ちりょう = 治療 'medical treatment'.
Wrong. じ is a real reading of 治 (政治 せいじ), but 治療 uses ち.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 療 is りょう, not りょ.
Wrong. 療 is read りょう, not りゅう. りゅう is the reading of kanji such as 流 and 留.

vocab.example: 歯{は}の治療{ちりょう}には時間{じかん}がかかる。
vocab.example_translation: Dental treatment takes time.

vocab.meaning: to receive, to undergo; to take (an exam)
vocab.example: 来年{らいねん}、大学{だいがく}の入学試験{にゅうがくしけん}を受{う}ける。
vocab.example_translation: I will take the university entrance exam next year.

vocab.example: 熱{ねつ}が高{たか}いので病院{びょういん}へ行{い}った。
vocab.example_translation: I had a high fever, so I went to the hospital.

vocab.example: この国{くに}は医療{いりょう}が進{すす}んでいる。
vocab.example_translation: This country has advanced medical care.

vocab.meaning: to get better, to be cured
vocab.example: 薬{くすり}を飲{の}んだら、風邪{かぜ}がすぐ治{なお}った。
vocab.example_translation: When I took the medicine, my cold got better quickly.

grammar.meaning: it has been decided that ~ (by others or by circumstances)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない form + ことになる (often ことになった)
grammar.example: 来月{らいげつ}から大阪{おおさか}で働{はたら}くことになった。
grammar.example_translation: It has been decided that I will work in Osaka from next month.

question: この冷蔵庫{れいぞうこ}は、買{か}ってから三年間{さんねんかん}の[[保証]]が付{つ}いている。
translation: This refrigerator comes with a three-year warranty from the date of purchase.
explanation: 保証 is read ほしょう and means 'guarantee, warranty'. 保 is a short ほ, as in 保存 ほぞん 'preservation' and 保険 ほけん 'insurance'; its kun'yomi is たもつ (保つ 'to keep'). 証 is read しょう, as in 証明 しょうめい 'proof' and 証拠 しょうこ 'evidence'. Be careful: three different words share the reading ほしょう. 保証 'guarantee', 保障 'security' (社会保障 'social security'), and 補償 'compensation'. In the exam you only need the reading, but knowing the three words helps in the orthography section too.
choice_notes: Wrong. 保 is a short ほ. (ほうしょう is 褒賞 / 報奨 'reward'.)
Wrong. 証 is read しょう without a dakuten.
Correct. ほしょう = 保証 'guarantee, warranty'.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 証 is しょう, not しょ.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}が正直{しょうじき}な人{ひと}だということは私{わたし}が保証{ほしょう}します。
vocab.example_translation: I guarantee that he is an honest person.

vocab.example: 牛乳{ぎゅうにゅう}を冷蔵庫{れいぞうこ}に入{い}れておいた。
vocab.example_translation: I put the milk in the refrigerator.

vocab.meaning: to come with, to be attached; to stick
vocab.example: このホテルの料金{りょうきん}には朝食{ちょうしょく}が付{つ}いている。
vocab.example_translation: This hotel's rate includes breakfast.

vocab.example: 身分{みぶん}を証明{しょうめい}するものを見{み}せてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please show me something that proves your identity.

grammar.meaning: after ~; since ~
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + から
grammar.example: 日本{にほん}に来{き}てから、三年{さんねん}が経{た}った。
grammar.example_translation: Three years have passed since I came to Japan.

question: 年{とし}を取{と}るにつれて、体力{たいりょく}が[[衰えて]]きた。
translation: As I have gotten older, my physical strength has declined.
explanation: 衰えて is the て-form of 衰える（おとろえる）'to weaken, to decline': 体力が衰える 'one's strength declines', 人気が衰える 'popularity fades'. The on'yomi is すい, as in 衰退 すいたい 'decline (of an industry, a town)' and 老衰 ろうすい 'old age, senility'. The kanji 衰 looks similar to 哀 (あい, 哀れ あわれ 'pity'), so be careful. All the distractors are real ichidan verbs that start with お and whose て-form ends in an e-sound + て (-えて or -れて), just like おとろえて; おとずれて is the most dangerous because it also starts with おと-.
choice_notes: Wrong. おとずれて is 訪れて, from 訪れる 'to visit'. It starts with おと- too, but it is a different verb.
Wrong. おびえて is 怯えて, from 怯える 'to be frightened'.
Wrong. おそれて is 恐れて, from 恐れる 'to fear'.
Correct. おとろえて = 衰えて, from 衰える 'to weaken, to decline'.

vocab.meaning: to weaken, to decline, to fade
vocab.example: 年{とし}とともに記憶力{きおくりょく}が衰{おとろ}える。
vocab.example_translation: Memory declines with age.

vocab.example: 祖母{そぼ}は年{とし}を取{と}っても元気{げんき}だ。
vocab.example_translation: My grandmother is healthy even though she has grown old.

vocab.example: マラソンには体力{たいりょく}が必要{ひつよう}だ。
vocab.example_translation: A marathon requires stamina.

vocab.example: 若者{わかもの}が減{へ}って、町{まち}の商店街{しょうてんがい}が衰退{すいたい}した。
vocab.example_translation: With fewer young people, the town's shopping street declined.

grammar.meaning: as ~ (changes), ... (also changes)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + につれて
grammar.example: 時間{じかん}が経{た}つにつれて、悲{かな}しみが薄{うす}れていった。
grammar.example_translation: As time passed, the sadness faded.

grammar.meaning: has become ~ / has started to ~ (a change up to now)
