grammar.formation: Verb て-form + くる
grammar.example: だんだん寒{さむ}くなってきた。
grammar.example_translation: It has gradually gotten colder.

question: 今年{ことし}は天気{てんき}に恵{めぐ}まれて、米{こめ}の[[収穫]]が多{おお}かった。
translation: This year we were blessed with good weather, and the rice harvest was large.
explanation: 収穫 is read しゅうかく and means 'harvest'; figuratively it also means 'a gain, something worthwhile' (今回の旅行は大きな収穫があった 'I gained a lot from this trip'). 収 is read しゅう with a long vowel, as in 収入 しゅうにゅう 'income' and 回収 かいしゅう 'collection'; its kun'yomi is おさめる (収める). 穫 is read かく and appears almost only in this word. The similar-looking 獲 (獲得 かくとく 'acquisition') is also かく. The distractors are real words: 主格 しゅかく 'nominative case', 修学 しゅうがく 'learning' (修学旅行 'school trip'), 集会 しゅうかい 'gathering'.
choice_notes: Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 収 is しゅう. (しゅかく is 主格 'nominative case'.)
Correct. しゅうかく = 収穫 'harvest'.
Wrong. しゅうがく is 修学 'learning'. 穫 is read かく without a dakuten.
Wrong. しゅうかい is 集会 'gathering, meeting'. 穫 is read かく.

vocab.example: 留学{りゅうがく}して一番{いちばん}の収穫{しゅうかく}は、友達{ともだち}ができたことだ。
vocab.example_translation: The biggest gain from studying abroad was making friends.

vocab.meaning: to be blessed with, to be fortunate in
vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は才能{さいのう}に恵{めぐ}まれている。
vocab.example_translation: He is blessed with talent.

vocab.example: この地方{ちほう}はおいしい米{こめ}で有名{ゆうめい}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This region is famous for its delicious rice.

vocab.example: 収入{しゅうにゅう}が増{ふ}えたので、引{ひ}っ越{こ}した。
vocab.example_translation: My income increased, so I moved.

grammar.meaning: to be blessed with ~
grammar.formation: Noun + に恵まれる
grammar.example: 旅行中{りょこうちゅう}は毎日{まいにち}いい天気{てんき}に恵{めぐ}まれた。
grammar.example_translation: We were blessed with good weather every day during the trip.

question: 彼{かれ}は家族{かぞく}のために、自分{じぶん}の趣味{しゅみ}を[[犠牲]]にした。
translation: He sacrificed his own hobbies for the sake of his family.
explanation: 犠牲 is read ぎせい and means 'sacrifice' (〜を犠牲にする 'to sacrifice ~') and also 'victim' (犠牲者 ぎせいしゃ 'victim'). 犠 is read ぎ and 牲 is read せい; both kanji appear almost only in this word. Both have the 牛 (ox) radical on the left, because the word originally meant animals offered to the gods. The trap ぎしょう comes from the similar-looking kanji 性, which can be read しょう (相性 あいしょう 'compatibility'), but 牲 is always せい. きせい is a real word too: 規制 'regulation' or 帰省 'going back to one's hometown'.
choice_notes: Correct. ぎせい = 犠牲 'sacrifice'.
Wrong. きせい is 規制 'regulation' or 帰省 'returning home'. 犠 is read ぎ with a dakuten.
Wrong. 牲 is read せい without a dakuten.
Wrong. しょう is a reading of the similar-looking kanji 性 (相性 あいしょう), not 牲. (ぎしょう is 偽証 'false testimony'.)

vocab.example: 睡眠{すいみん}を犠牲{ぎせい}にして勉強{べんきょう}するのはよくない。
vocab.example_translation: It is not good to study at the expense of sleep.

vocab.example: 週末{しゅうまつ}は家族{かぞく}と過{す}ごすことが多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: I often spend weekends with my family.

vocab.example: 自分{じぶん}のことは自分{じぶん}でしなさい。
vocab.example_translation: Take care of your own things yourself.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}の趣味{しゅみ}は写真{しゃしん}を撮{と}ることだ。
vocab.example_translation: My hobby is taking photos.

vocab.example: その事故{じこ}で多{おお}くの犠牲者{ぎせいしゃ}が出{で}た。
vocab.example_translation: There were many victims in that accident.

grammar.meaning: for the sake of ~, for ~
grammar.formation: Noun + のために
grammar.example: 子{こ}どもの将来{しょうらい}のために、お金{かね}をためている。
grammar.example_translation: I am saving money for my children's future.

grammar.meaning: to make ~ into ~, to turn ~ into ~ (犠牲にする 'to sacrifice')
grammar.formation: Noun A + を + noun B + にする
grammar.example: 空{あ}いている部屋{へや}を書斎{しょさい}にした。
grammar.example_translation: I turned the empty room into a study.

question: 初{はじ}めて会{あ}う人{ひと}の前{まえ}で歌{うた}うのは、少{すこ}し[[抵抗]]がある。
translation: I feel a little reluctant to sing in front of people I am meeting for the first time.
explanation: 抵抗 is read ていこう. Its basic meaning is 'resistance' (警察に抵抗する 'to resist the police'; 電気抵抗 'electrical resistance'), and 〜に抵抗がある means 'to feel reluctant / uncomfortable about ~'. 抵 is read てい, as in 大抵 たいてい 'usually, mostly'. 抗 is read こう, as in 反抗 はんこう 'rebellion' and 対抗 たいこう 'rivalry'. The trap たいこう is the real word 対抗, which also has the meaning 'opposing', so it fits the 'resist' image. But 抵 is read てい.
choice_notes: Wrong. たいこう is 対抗 'opposition, rivalry'. Its meaning is close, but 抵 is read てい, not たい.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 抗 is こう, not こ.
Wrong. 抵 is read てい without a dakuten.
Correct. ていこう = 抵抗 'resistance; reluctance'.

vocab.meaning: resistance; reluctance (〜に抵抗がある 'to feel reluctant about')
vocab.example: 犯人{はんにん}は警察{けいさつ}に抵抗{ていこう}したが、すぐに捕{つか}まった。
vocab.example_translation: The criminal resisted the police but was soon caught.

vocab.example: 初{はじ}めて富士山{ふじさん}を見{み}たとき、感動{かんどう}した。
vocab.example_translation: When I saw Mt. Fuji for the first time, I was moved.

vocab.example: 日曜日{にちようび}は大抵{たいてい}家{いえ}にいる。
vocab.example_translation: I am usually at home on Sundays.

vocab.example: 隣{となり}のクラスに対抗{たいこう}して、毎日{まいにち}練習{れんしゅう}した。
vocab.example_translation: We practiced every day to compete against the class next door.

grammar.meaning: doing ~ is ... (の turns the verb phrase into the topic)
grammar.formation: Verb plain form + のは + comment
grammar.example: 一人{ひとり}で旅行{りょこう}するのは楽{たの}しい。
grammar.example_translation: Traveling alone is fun.

question: 学費{がくひ}を[[稼ぐ]]ために、夜{よる}はレストランでアルバイトをしている。
translation: To earn my tuition, I work part-time at a restaurant in the evenings.
explanation: 稼ぐ is read かせぐ and means 'to earn (money)'; it can also mean 'to gain, to buy (time, points)': 時間を稼ぐ 'to buy time'. Its noun form is 稼ぎ かせぎ 'earnings'. The on'yomi is か, as in 稼働 かどう 'operation (of a machine or factory)'. The right side of 稼 is 家 (か), which is a good memory hook for the on'yomi. The distractors are real godan verbs ending in -ぐ: 担ぐ かつぐ and 騒ぐ さわぐ. Also note that the せ has no dakuten.
choice_notes: Wrong. かつぐ is 担ぐ 'to carry on one's shoulder'. Different kanji.
Wrong. The せ has no dakuten: かせぐ, not かぜぐ.
Correct. かせぐ = 稼ぐ 'to earn'.
Wrong. さわぐ is 騒ぐ 'to make noise, to make a fuss'. Different kanji.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}は週末{しゅうまつ}も働{はたら}いてお金{かね}を稼{かせ}いでいる。
vocab.example_translation: He works on weekends too to earn money.

vocab.example: 大学{だいがく}の学費{がくひ}は高{たか}い。
vocab.example_translation: University tuition is expensive.

vocab.example: 駅前{えきまえ}のコンビニでアルバイトを始{はじ}めた。
vocab.example_translation: I started a part-time job at the convenience store in front of the station.

vocab.example: 今月{こんげつ}は稼{かせ}ぎが少{すく}なかった。
vocab.example_translation: My earnings were low this month.

grammar.meaning: in order to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ために / noun + のために
grammar.example: 試験{しけん}に合格{ごうかく}するために、毎日{まいにち}勉強{べんきょう}している。
grammar.example_translation: I study every day in order to pass the exam.

question: 工場{こうじょう}から流{なが}れ出{で}た排水{はいすい}によって、川{かわ}が[[汚染]]された。
translation: The river was polluted by wastewater that flowed out of the factory.
explanation: 汚染 is read おせん and means 'pollution, contamination': 大気汚染 'air pollution', 水質汚染 'water pollution'. 汚 is a short お, as in 汚職 おしょく 'corruption'; its kun'yomi are きたない (汚い 'dirty') and よごれる (汚れる 'to get dirty'). 染 is read せん, as in 感染 かんせん 'infection' and 伝染 でんせん 'contagion'; its kun'yomi is そめる (染める 'to dye'). Traps: お膳 おぜん 'meal tray' (dakuten), 応戦 おうせん (long vowel), and かんせん 感染, which uses the same 染. Also, 汚 looks like 汗 (あせ 'sweat'; on'yomi かん).
choice_notes: Correct. おせん = 汚染 'pollution'.
Wrong. 染 is read せん without a dakuten. (おぜん is お膳 'meal tray'.)
Wrong. 汚 is a short お. (おうせん is 応戦 'fighting back'.)
Wrong. かんせん is 感染 'infection'. It shares 染, but the first kanji is 感. 汚 is read お (the similar-looking 汗 is read かん).

vocab.example: 大気{たいき}の汚染{おせん}が問題{もんだい}になっている。
vocab.example_translation: Air pollution has become a problem.

vocab.example: 父{ちち}は自動車{じどうしゃ}の工場{こうじょう}で働{はたら}いている。
vocab.example_translation: My father works in a car factory.

vocab.meaning: to flow out, to run out
vocab.example: 傷{きず}から血{ち}が流{なが}れ出{で}た。
vocab.example_translation: Blood flowed out of the wound.

vocab.example: 台所{だいどころ}の排水{はいすい}が詰{つ}まった。
vocab.example_translation: The kitchen drain got clogged.

vocab.example: 雨{あめ}の中{なか}を歩{ある}いて靴{くつ}が汚{よご}れた。
vocab.example_translation: My shoes got dirty from walking in the rain.

grammar.meaning: by ~ (marks the cause or doer in a passive sentence)
grammar.formation: Noun + によって + passive verb
grammar.example: この寺{てら}は有名{ゆうめい}な建築家{けんちくか}によって建{た}てられた。
grammar.example_translation: This temple was built by a famous architect.

question: 日頃{ひごろ}から[[災害]]に備{そな}えて、避難場所{ひなんばしょ}を確認{かくにん}しておくべきだ。
translation: You should check evacuation sites in your everyday life to be prepared for disasters.
explanation: 災害 is read さいがい and means 'disaster' (自然災害 'natural disaster'). 災 is read さい, as in 火災 かさい 'fire' and 震災 しんさい 'earthquake disaster'; its kun'yomi is わざわい (災い 'misfortune'). 害 is read がい with a dakuten, as in 被害 ひがい 'damage' and 損害 そんがい 'loss'. The traps are real words: 再会 / 再開 さいかい 'reunion / resumption' (no dakuten) and 栽培 さいばい 'cultivation'. ざいがい simply puts a wrong dakuten on 災.
choice_notes: Wrong. さいかい is 再会 'reunion' or 再開 'resumption'. 害 is read がい with a dakuten.
Correct. さいがい = 災害 'disaster'.
Wrong. 災 is read さい without a dakuten.
Wrong. さいばい is 栽培 'growing (plants), cultivation'. 害 is read がい.

vocab.example: 日本{にほん}は自然災害{しぜんさいがい}が多{おお}い国{くに}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Japan is a country with many natural disasters.

vocab.example: 日頃{ひごろ}の練習{れんしゅう}の成果{せいか}が出{で}た。
vocab.example_translation: The results of everyday practice showed.

vocab.example: 近所{きんじょ}の小学校{しょうがっこう}が避難場所{ひなんばしょ}になっている。
vocab.example_translation: The local elementary school serves as an evacuation site.

vocab.example: 送{おく}る前{まえ}に、宛先{あてさき}をもう一度{いちど}確認{かくにん}した。
vocab.example_translation: I checked the address once more before sending it.

vocab.example: 試験{しけん}に備{そな}えて早{はや}く寝{ね}た。
vocab.example_translation: I went to bed early to prepare for the exam.

grammar.meaning: should ~, ought to ~ (strong opinion about what is right)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + べきだ (する → するべき / すべき)
grammar.example: 若{わか}いうちにいろいろな経験{けいけん}をするべきだ。
grammar.example_translation: You should have many kinds of experiences while you are young.

grammar.meaning: to do ~ in advance
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + おく
grammar.example: 旅行{りょこう}の前{まえ}に、ホテルを予約{よやく}しておいた。
grammar.example_translation: I booked a hotel in advance before the trip.

grammar.meaning: in preparation for ~
grammar.formation: Noun + に備えて
grammar.example: 冬{ふゆ}に備{そな}えて、暖{あたた}かい服{ふく}を買{か}った。
grammar.example_translation: I bought warm clothes to get ready for winter.

question: 彼{かれ}の返事{へんじ}はいつも[[曖昧]]で、本当{ほんとう}の気持{きも}ちが分{わ}からない。
translation: His replies are always vague, so I can't tell what he really feels.
explanation: 曖昧 is read あいまい and means 'vague, ambiguous, unclear': 曖昧な返事 'a vague answer', 記憶が曖昧だ 'my memory is fuzzy'. 曖 is read あい; it contains 愛 (あい 'love'), which is a nice memory hook. 昧 is read まい, as in 読書三昧 どくしょざんまい 'doing nothing but reading' (三昧 is さんまい on its own and becomes ざんまい as a suffix). The traps come from similar-looking kanji: 味 み (taste) shares the part 未 with 昧, and 末 まつ (end) looks almost the same as 未. The voiced ばい is simply wrong.
choice_notes: Wrong. み is the reading of the similar-looking kanji 味 (意味 いみ). 昧 is read まい.
Wrong. 昧 is read まい, not ばい.
Correct. あいまい = 曖昧 'vague, ambiguous'.
Wrong. まつ is the reading of 末 (週末 しゅうまつ), which looks like the 未 part of 昧. 昧 is read まい.

vocab.example: 曖昧{あいまい}な答{こた}えではなく、はっきり言{い}ってください。
vocab.example_translation: Please say it clearly instead of giving a vague answer.

vocab.example: 手紙{てがみ}の返事{へんじ}がまだ来{こ}ない。
vocab.example_translation: I still haven't received a reply to my letter.

vocab.example: 本当{ほんとう}のことを教{おし}えてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please tell me the truth.

vocab.example: 相手{あいて}の気持{きも}ちを考{かんが}えて話{はな}そう。
vocab.example_translation: Let's speak while thinking about the other person's feelings.

grammar.meaning: ~, so ... (the て-form shows a cause; な-adjectives and nouns use で)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form / い-adj くて / な-adj・noun + で
grammar.example: 風邪{かぜ}を引{ひ}いて、学校{がっこう}を休{やす}んだ。
grammar.example_translation: I caught a cold, so I stayed home from school.

question: 大雨{おおあめ}が降{ふ}ったあと、川{かわ}の水{みず}が茶色{ちゃいろ}く[[濁って]]いた。
translation: After the heavy rain, the river water was muddy and brown.
explanation: 濁って is the て-form of 濁る（にごる）'to become muddy, cloudy, impure'. Its opposite is 澄む すむ 'to become clear'. The on'yomi is だく, as in 濁音 だくおん 'voiced sound' and 濁点 だくてん, the ゛ mark itself, which is a fun connection because the answer depends on that mark: に・ご, not に・こ. The trap にぶって is 鈍って, from 鈍る 'to become dull', and くもって is 曇って, from 曇る 'to become cloudy'. 曇る is used for the sky or glass (空が曇る, 眼鏡が曇る), but for water we say 濁る.
choice_notes: Wrong. にぶって is 鈍って, from 鈍る 'to become dull, to weaken'.
Wrong. The dakuten is missing: it is ご, not こ.
Wrong. くもって is 曇って, from 曇る 'to become cloudy'. It is used for the sky or glass, not for river water.
Correct. にごって = 濁って, from 濁る 'to become muddy, cloudy'.

vocab.meaning: to become muddy, cloudy, impure; to be voiced (a sound)
vocab.example: 池{いけ}の水{みず}が濁{にご}って、魚{さかな}が見{み}えない。
vocab.example_translation: The pond water is cloudy, so I can't see the fish.

vocab.example: 大雨{おおあめ}のため、試合{しあい}は中止{ちゅうし}になった。
vocab.example_translation: The match was canceled because of heavy rain.

vocab.example: 茶色{ちゃいろ}い犬{いぬ}が走{はし}っている。
vocab.example_translation: A brown dog is running.

vocab.example: 「か」に濁点{だくてん}を付{つ}けると「が」になる。
vocab.example_translation: If you add a dakuten to か, it becomes が.

vocab.example: 山{やま}の空気{くうき}は澄{す}んでいる。
vocab.example_translation: The mountain air is clear.

grammar.meaning: after ~
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + あと（で）/ noun + の + あと（で）
grammar.example: 食事{しょくじ}をしたあとで、散歩{さんぽ}に行{い}った。
grammar.example_translation: After eating, I went for a walk.

grammar.meaning: turns an い-adjective into an adverb (茶色い → 茶色く濁る 'turn muddy brown')
grammar.formation: い-adjective without い + く + verb
grammar.example: 髪{かみ}を短{みじか}く切{き}った。
grammar.example_translation: I cut my hair short.

question: この店{みせ}では、週末{しゅうまつ}に働{はたら}けるアルバイトを[[募集]]している。
translation: This shop is recruiting part-time workers who can work on weekends.
explanation: 募集 is read ぼしゅう and means 'recruitment, call for applications' (社員募集 'now hiring staff', アルバイト募集中 'part-timers wanted'). 募 is a short ぼ with a dakuten, as in 応募 おうぼ 'applying' and 募金 ぼきん 'fundraising'; its kun'yomi is つのる (募る 'to invite, to raise'). 集 is read しゅう with a long vowel, as in 集合 しゅうごう 'gathering'; its kun'yomi is あつめる (集める). Similar-looking kanji: 墓 ぼ (墓地 ぼち 'cemetery') and 暮 ぼ (歳暮 せいぼ). The traps change the vowel length or remove the dakuten (補習 ほしゅう 'extra lessons').
choice_notes: Correct. ぼしゅう = 募集 'recruitment'.
Wrong. 募 is a short ぼ, not ぼう.
Wrong. ほしゅう is 補習 'supplementary lessons' or 補修 'repair'. 募 is read ぼ with a dakuten.
Wrong. The long vowel is missing: 集 is しゅう, not しゅ.

vocab.example: 会社{かいしゃ}のホームページで社員{しゃいん}を募集{ぼしゅう}している。
vocab.example_translation: The company is recruiting staff on its website.

vocab.example: 週末{しゅうまつ}は友達{ともだち}とテニスをする。
vocab.example_translation: I play tennis with friends on weekends.

vocab.example: 兄{あに}は銀行{ぎんこう}で働{はたら}いている。
vocab.example_translation: My older brother works at a bank.

vocab.example: 学生{がくせい}のときは本屋{ほんや}でアルバイトをしていた。
vocab.example_translation: When I was a student, I worked part-time at a bookstore.

vocab.example: スピーチコンテストに応募{おうぼ}した。
vocab.example_translation: I applied for the speech contest.

grammar.meaning: can ~, to be able to ~ (働ける 'can work')
grammar.formation: Group 1: change the final う-sound to え + る (働く → 働ける); Group 2: stem + られる; する → できる
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は三{みっ}つの言語{げんご}が話{はな}せる。
grammar.example_translation: He can speak three languages.

question: 社長{しゃちょう}の厳{きび}しい言葉{ことば}のあと、会議室{かいぎしつ}に長{なが}い[[沈黙]]が続{つづ}いた。
translation: After the company president's harsh words, a long silence continued in the meeting room.
explanation: 沈黙 is read ちんもく and means 'silence (not speaking)'. 沈 is read ちん, as in 沈没 ちんぼつ 'sinking (of a ship)'; its kun'yomi is しずむ (沈む 'to sink'). 黙 is read もく, as in 黙認 もくにん 'tacit approval' and 寡黙 かもく 'quiet, reticent'; its kun'yomi is だまる (黙る 'to be silent'). The traps: しずもく mixes the kun'yomi しず- of 沈む into an on'yomi compound; ちんぼく comes from 墨 (ぼく 'ink'), which shares the 黒 part with 黙; じんもく uses じん, a rare reading of 沈 found only in a few words such as 沈丁花 じんちょうげ 'daphne', not in 沈黙.
choice_notes: Wrong. 沈黙 uses ちん. じん is a rare reading of 沈 (沈丁花 じんちょうげ 'daphne'), not used here.
Correct. ちんもく = 沈黙 'silence'.
Wrong. ぼく is the reading of 墨 'ink', which shares the 黒 part with 黙. 黙 is read もく.
Wrong. しず- is the kun'yomi of 沈む, but the compound 沈黙 uses the on'yomi ちん.

vocab.example: 彼{かれ}はしばらく沈黙{ちんもく}したあと、ゆっくり話{はな}し始{はじ}めた。
vocab.example_translation: He was silent for a while, then slowly began to speak.

vocab.example: 社長{しゃちょう}は毎朝{まいあさ}八時{はちじ}に会社{かいしゃ}に来{く}る。
vocab.example_translation: The president comes to the office at eight every morning.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}の父{ちち}はとても厳{きび}しかった。
vocab.example_translation: My father was very strict.

vocab.example: 会議室{かいぎしつ}は三階{さんがい}にあります。
vocab.example_translation: The meeting room is on the third floor.

vocab.meaning: to be silent, to stop talking
vocab.example: 先生{せんせい}に叱{しか}られて、彼{かれ}は黙{だま}ってしまった。
vocab.example_translation: After being scolded by the teacher, he fell silent.

vocab.meaning: to continue, to last, to go on
vocab.example: 暑{あつ}い日{ひ}が一週間{いっしゅうかん}続{つづ}いている。
vocab.example_translation: Hot days have continued for a week.

grammar.meaning: after ~ (a noun)
grammar.formation: Noun + の + あと（で）
grammar.example: 授業{じゅぎょう}のあとで、図書館{としょかん}に行{い}く。
grammar.example_translation: I will go to the library after class.

question: 彼女{かのじょ}は[[優秀]]な成績{せいせき}で大学{だいがく}を卒業{そつぎょう}した。
translation: She graduated from university with excellent grades.
explanation: 優秀 is read ゆうしゅう and means 'excellent, outstanding (person, grades, work)'. Both kanji have long vowels: 優 is ゆう, as in 優先 ゆうせん 'priority' and 女優 じょゆう 'actress' (kun'yomi やさしい 優しい 'kind', すぐれる 優れる 'to excel'), and 秀 is しゅう, as in 秀才 しゅうさい 'brilliant student'. The traps drop one of the long vowels, or swap in 優勝 ゆうしょう 'winning a championship', a very common word that starts the same way.
choice_notes: Wrong. The final long vowel is missing: 秀 is しゅう, not しゅ.
Wrong. The first long vowel is missing: 優 is ゆう, not ゆ.
Wrong. ゆうしょう is 優勝 'winning the championship'. 秀 is read しゅう, not しょう.
Correct. ゆうしゅう = 優秀 'excellent'.

vocab.example: この会社{かいしゃ}には優秀{ゆうしゅう}な社員{しゃいん}が多{おお}い。
vocab.example_translation: This company has many excellent employees.

vocab.example: 今学期{こんがっき}は数学{すうがく}の成績{せいせき}が上{あ}がった。
vocab.example_translation: My math grades went up this semester.

vocab.example: 兄{あに}は去年{きょねん}高校{こうこう}を卒業{そつぎょう}した。
vocab.example_translation: My older brother graduated from high school last year.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}たちのチームが大会{たいかい}で優勝{ゆうしょう}した。
vocab.example_translation: Our team won the tournament.

grammar.meaning: with ~, by ~ (the means or condition of an action)
grammar.formation: Noun + で
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}はトップの成績{せいせき}で試験{しけん}に合格{ごうかく}した。
grammar.example_translation: He passed the exam with top marks.

question: 花火大会{はなびたいかい}の日{ひ}は、[[臨時]]の電車{でんしゃ}が運行{うんこう}される。
translation: On the day of the fireworks festival, extra (special) trains are run.
explanation: 臨時 is read りんじ and means 'temporary, special, extra (not regular)': 臨時ニュース 'breaking news', 臨時休業 'temporarily closed'. 臨 is read りん, as in 臨場感 りんじょうかん 'sense of being there, realism'; its kun'yomi is のぞむ (臨む 'to face, to attend'). 時 is read じ with a dakuten in on'yomi words like 時間 じかん and 当時 とうじ. The traps: the unvoiced し, the kun'yomi とき (voiced to どき in words like 昼時 ひるどき) mixed into an on'yomi compound, and りんじょう from 臨場 'being on the scene', which uses 場 instead of 時.
choice_notes: Wrong. 時 is read じ with a dakuten, not し.
Wrong. とき / どき is the kun'yomi of 時, but the compound 臨時 uses the on'yomi じ.
Correct. りんじ = 臨時 'temporary, special'.
Wrong. りんじょう is 臨場 (as in 臨場感 'realism'), written with 場, not 時.

vocab.example: 今日{きょう}は店{みせ}が臨時休業{りんじきゅうぎょう}だった。
vocab.example_translation: The shop was temporarily closed today.

vocab.example: 夏{なつ}になると各地{かくち}で花火大会{はなびたいかい}が開{ひら}かれる。

question: 彼{かれ}は有名{ゆうめい}になっても、[[謙虚]]な態度{たいど}を忘{わす}れなかった。
translation: Even after becoming famous, he never lost his modest attitude.
explanation: 謙虚 is read けんきょ and means 'modest, humble'. 謙 is read けん, as in 謙遜 けんそん 'modesty' and 謙譲語 けんじょうご 'humble language (a type of 敬語)'. 虚 is read きょ with a SHORT vowel, as in 虚偽 きょぎ 'falsehood'; its kun'yomi is むなしい (虚しい 'empty, futile'). 虚 has a rare reading こ (虚空 こくう 'empty sky'), which is the trap けんこ. The other traps add a long vowel (けんきょう) or a dakuten (げんきょ).
choice_notes: Correct. けんきょ = 謙虚 'modest, humble'.
Wrong. 虚 is a short きょ, not きょう.
Wrong. 謙 is read けん without a dakuten.
Wrong. こ is a rare reading of 虚 (虚空 こくう), but 謙虚 uses きょ.

vocab.example: 失敗{しっぱい}したときは、謙虚{けんきょ}に人{ひと}の意見{いけん}を聞{き}くべきだ。

question: 明日{あした}の発表{はっぴょう}の準備{じゅんび}のために、昨夜{さくや}は[[徹夜]]した。
translation: I stayed up all night last night to prepare for tomorrow's presentation.
explanation: 徹夜 is read てつや and means 'staying up all night'. 徹 is read てつ, as in 徹底 てってい 'thoroughness' and 貫徹 かんてつ 'carrying through'. Do not confuse it with 撤 (てつ, as in 撤退 てったい 'withdrawal'): they look alike and share the reading. 夜 is read や in on'yomi words, as in 今夜 こんや 'tonight' and 深夜 しんや 'late at night'; its kun'yomi are よる and よ (夜中 よなか 'middle of the night'). So てつよ and てつよる wrongly mix in the kun'yomi. てっや is impossible because a small っ is not used before や.
choice_notes: Wrong. よ is a kun'yomi of 夜 (夜中 よなか), but 徹夜 uses the on'yomi や.
Correct. てつや = 徹夜 'staying up all night'.
Wrong. There is no small っ. A small っ cannot come before や.
Wrong. よる is the kun'yomi of 夜 used alone, not in this compound.

vocab.example: 徹夜{てつや}で勉強{べんきょう}しても、あまり覚{おぼ}えられない。
vocab.example_translation: Even if you study all night, you can't remember much.
